The control strain was ineffective, and PPAR-α inhibition abolished both intestinal and hepatic protection. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that engineered probiotics acting as "living drug factories" can target the gut-liver axis via localized PEA biosynthesis, restoring barrier integrity and limiting hepatic inflammatory and fibrogenic signaling in chronic colitis.

articles.title: Integrative network toxicology and pharmacology reveal that kaempferol alleviates BaP-triggered pulmonary fibrosis via suppressing Ras/COX-2-dependent cellular senescence.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a chronic, progressive lung disease. Benzo[a]pyrene (BaP), a major constituent of cigarette smoke and air pollution, has been closely associated with pulmonary fibrosis. However, its molecular mechanism remains unclear. The natural flavonoid kaempferol possesses anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. However, its effects and mechanisms in BaP-induced pulmonary fibrosis remain unclear. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to predict potential targets of BaP-induced fibrosis and kaempferol intervention in BaP-induced IPF, and to validate whether kaempferol reverses BaP-induced epithelial senescence and fibrosis via the Ras/COX-2 signaling pathway in vitro. METHODS: Network toxicology, network pharmacology, machine learning, and molecular docking were integrated to predict potential targets of BaP-induced fibrosis and kaempferol intervention, followed by GO and KEGG pathway enrichment analyses. Additionally, virtual knockout analysis was performed to explore the regulatory relationships among Ras, COX-2, and cellular senescence. MLE-12 cells were used as an in vitro model, and senescence-related indicators were assessed by SA-β-gal staining, Western blot, and ELISA. RESULTS: KEGG enrichment analysis revealed that these targets were significantly enriched in the Ras signaling pathway. Molecular docking confirmed that kaempferol exhibited good binding affinity for the above target proteins. Cell experiments demonstrated that BaP significantly promoted cellular senescence and activated Ras and COX-2. Kaempferol treatment effectively reversed these changes. CONCLUSION: This study reveals that BaP promotes IPF by inducing epithelial cell senescence via the Ras/COX-2 signaling pathway. Kaempferol may exert anti-fibrotic effects by counteracting this pathway-mediated senescence. These findings provide a theoretical basis for the pulmonary fibrosis effects of BaP and support kaempferol as a potential anti-fibrotic agent.

articles.title: A real-world pharmacovigilance study of FDA adverse event reporting system events for bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide (B/F/TAF) is a widely used antiretroviral regimen, but its real-world long-term safety profile in diverse populations remains incompletely characterized. METHODS: We analyzed adverse drug signals from the FAERS database (2018-2025) with B/F/TAF as the primary suspected drug. Disproportionality analyses using reporting odds ratio (ROR), proportional reporting ratio (PRR), Bayesian confidence propagation neural network (BCPNN), and multi-item gamma Poisson shrinker (MGPS) algorithms were performed to detect safety signals. RESULTS: A total of 6,816 case reports and 13,853 adverse events were included. The highest numbers of reports were related to "Injury, poisoning and procedural complications" (n = 1,792), followed by "General disorders and administration site conditions" (n = 1,726) and "Investigations" (n = 1,499). The System Organ Classes (SOCs) meeting all four disproportionality criteria were "Congenital, familial and genetic disorders" and "Pregnancy, puerperium and perinatal conditions." The most frequently reported preferred terms were weight increase (408 cases), product dose omission (242 cases), and maternal exposure during pregnancy (202 cases), while the strongest signals by ROR were viral load increased (ROR 160.14), CD4 lymphocytes decreased (ROR 124.60), and immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (ROR 88.12). Overall, 37.94% of events occurred within the first month of treatment, and 17.49% occurred after one year. CONCLUSION: These pharmacovigilance signals merit clinical awareness, particularly regarding metabolic monitoring, virologic/immunologic parameters (which likely reflect treatment response rather than drug toxicity), and pregnancy exposure reporting. Events occurred both early and late, reinforcing the necessity of longitudinal pharmacovigilance for this widely used antiretroviral regimen. However, these findings are exploratory and should not be interpreted as confirmed causal associations.

articles.title: A pectic polysaccharide from Lonicera japonica alleviates DNCB-induced atopic dermatitis-like inflammation associated with gut microbial and metabolic alterations and reduced cutaneous JAK2/STAT3 activation and Th17 responses.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Lonicera japonica Thunb. (Jin Yin Hua) is a traditional medicinal herb widely used in East Asia for inflammatory disorders and is commonly included in herbal prescriptions for atopic dermatitis (AD). WLJP-025p, a homogeneous pectic polysaccharide isolated from Lonicera japonica, has shown anti-inflammatory and anti-AD potential, but its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic effect of WLJP-025p on DNCB-induced AD-like dermatitis in mice and to investigate associated changes in epidermal barrier dysfunction, Th17/IL-17A-associated inflammation, JAK2/STAT3 signaling, and gut microbial and metabolic profiles. MATERIALS AND METHODS: An AD-like mouse model was established in BALB/c mice by repeated application of 2,4-dinitrochlorobenzene (DNCB). WLJP-025p was orally administered at 30 or 60 mg/kg during the challenge phase, and topical dexamethasone was used as a reference anti-inflammatory control. Disease severity was assessed by skin appearance, dermatitis score, ear thickness, serum biomarkers, and histopathological examination. Skin barrier and inflammation-related proteins were evaluated by immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, Western blotting, and flow cytometry. Colonic injury was examined by hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) and Alcian blue-periodic acid-Schiff (AB-PAS) staining. Fecal metagenomic and metabolomic analyses were conducted to characterize gut microbial and metabolic changes. RESULTS: WLJP-025p significantly alleviated DNCB-induced AD-like lesions, as evidenced by reduced erythema, scaling, excoriation, ear swelling, dermatitis scores, epidermal hyperplasia, and mast cell infiltration. WLJP-025p decreased serum IgE, IL-1β, IL-6, and IL-17A levels. It restored filaggrin (FLG) expression and suppressed thymic stromal lymphopoietin (TSLP) expression in skin lesions, indicating improved epidermal barrier function. WLJP-025p also reduced the proportions of splenic CD3+CD4+IL-17A+ T cells and suppressed cutaneous IL-17A-related inflammatory mediators, including CCR6 and CCL20. These changes were accompanied by decreased phosphorylation of JAK2 and STAT3 in lesional skin. In addition, WLJP-025p alleviated DNCB-associated colonic injury and was accompanied by changes in gut microbial and metabolic profiles. CONCLUSION: WLJP-025p exerted protective effects against DNCB-induced AD-like dermatitis. Treatment was accompanied by restoration of epidermal barrier-related markers, reduced JAK2/STAT3 activation and Th17/IL-17A-associated inflammatory signaling, improved gut barrier integrity, and alterations in gut microbial and fecal metabolite profiles. These findings indicate that oral WLJP-025p treatment is associated with concurrent intestinal and cutaneous changes in this AD-like model.

articles.title: Cardioprotective Effects of Xin-Shu-Ning Tablets against Myocardial Ischemia: Involvement of Protein Kinase B-Related Signaling in Apoptosis and Pyroptosis.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Xin-Shu-Ning Tablets (XSNT) are traditionally used to promote blood circulation and resolve blood stasis, including for coronary heart disease-associated angina. Their cardioprotective mechanisms and bioactive constituents remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to evaluate the cardioprotection of XSNT against myocardial ischemia and to investigate its underlying mechanisms and candidate bioactive constituents. MATERIALS AND METHODS: XSNT was evaluated in myocardial infarction (MI) mice using echocardiography, biochemical assays, histopathology, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence. Proteomics and prior network pharmacology guided PI3K/AKT analysis. H9c2 cells underwent 8 h of oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD), with MK-2206 used to assess AKT involvement. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, cellular thermal shift assays, and cellular experiments were used to evaluate the candidates. RESULTS: XSNT improved cardiac function and reduced myocardial injury in MI mice. Reduced TUNEL staining and changes in Bcl-2/Bax and cleaved caspase-3 supported attenuation of apoptosis, while reductions in inflammasome- and GSDMD-related proteins indicated decreased pyroptosis-related signaling. These effects accompanied increased AKT phosphorylation and reduced NF-κB activation. XSNT produced similar responses in OGD-challenged H9c2 cells, and MK-2206 partially attenuated these effects. Puerarin showed a potential interaction with AKT and reproduced some cellular effects of XSNT, which were also attenuated by MK-2206. CONCLUSION: XSNT attenuated myocardial injury and distinct apoptosis- and pyroptosis-related responses, with pharmacological evidence supporting AKT involvement. Puerarin represents a candidate bioactive constituent. This study has several limitations, including the unclear cellular sources of myocardial pyroptosis-related signals, the lack of genetic validation of AKT involvement, and the need for further confirmation in primary cardiomyocytes.

articles.title: Pretreatment with Feining Granules Mitigates LPS-Induced Lung Injury in Mice: Pharmacological and Serum Metabolomics Evidence.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: The Chinese patent medicine preparation Feining Granules (FNKL), formerly known as Fanhuncao Granules, is prepared from Fanhuncao, the dried aerial parts of Jacobaea cannabifolia or Jacobaea litvinovii. FNKL is traditionally used to relieve cough and promote expectoration and is approved for cough associated with chronic bronchitis. This use, together with its reported anti-inflammatory activity, provided the basis for examining FNKL in LPS-induced lung injury. AIM OF THE STUDY: To obtain a UHPLC-HRMS-based chemical profile of FNKL and assess its pretreatment effects in LPS-stimulated cells and LPS-challenged mice, extending previous FNKL research from chronic bronchitis to experimental acute lung injury. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A 70% ethanol extract was profiled by UHPLC-Q Exactive Orbitrap HRMS, whereas water-reconstituted FNKL was used in cellular experiments. Network pharmacology and metabolomics explored candidate targets and pathways. Effects were assessed in LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 and MLE-12 cells and in BALB/c mice assigned to control, LPS, three FNKL doses (0.975-3.9 g/kg/day), or dexamethasone (n = 10/group). Mice were pretreated orally for 7 days before intranasal LPS challenge. RESULTS: Sixty-six constituents were putatively annotated, mainly flavonoids, organic acids, and alkaloids. FNKL lowered IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α, and nitrite concentrations in RAW264.7 cell culture supernatants. At 1 mg/mL, FNKL exposure was associated with a lower apoptotic-cell percentage in MLE-12 cells than in cells exposed to LPS alone (7.42 ± 1.25% vs. 12.25 ± 1.75%; P < 0.01) and higher E-cadherin fluorescence intensity. In mice, pretreatment alleviated histological lung injury and reduced BALF IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-18. Serum metabolomics indicated candidate lipid- and energy-related changes. Protein analyses showed changes in markers related to inflammatory and metabolic signaling, apoptosis, and pyroptosis. CONCLUSIONS: FNKL pretreatment alleviated experimental LPS-induced lung injury, accompanied by changes in inflammatory signaling, serum metabolism, and cell-death-related markers. Causal mechanisms and safety require further investigation.

articles.title: Banxia Xiexin Decoction attenuates ethanol-induced acute gastric mucosal injury and gastric dysmotility: an integrated pharmacological and transcriptomic study.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Banxia Xiexin Decoction (BXD), a classical formula for gastric dysmotility. Ethanol-induced acute gastric injury causes mucosal damage and dysmotility; whether BXD improves this is unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: To investigate whether BXD alleviates gastric dysmotility in ethanol-induced acute gastric mucosal injury and its possible link to interstitial cells of Cajal (ICC) autophagy and PI3K/AKT/mTOR. MATERIALS AND METHODS: An ethanol-induced acute gastric mucosal injury rat model was established. We assessed gastric injury grossly and histologically and measured gastric emptying by the phenol red method. ICC integrity, autophagic markers, and PI3K/AKT/mTOR proteins were assessed by immunofluorescence, Western blot, and transmission electron microscopy. Network pharmacology and transcriptomics predicted pathways; we validated LY294002 in vitro. RESULTS: BXD dose-dependently attenuated ethanol-induced gastric mucosal injury; high and medium doses improved gastric emptying and preserved ICC network integrity. Ethanol induced autophagic substrate and vacuole accumulation in ICC, which BXD reduced, although a serum contribution cannot be excluded. These effects may involve PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling. Network pharmacology and transcriptomics suggested this axis as a candidate pathway; LY294002 partially attenuated BXD-induced mTOR phosphorylation in vitro, suggesting a contributory but not causal role of PI3K activity in reducing autophagic substrate accumulation. CONCLUSION: BXD reduced gastric mucosal injury and improved gastric motility, with preserved ICC network integrity and reduced autophagic substrate accumulation in ICC. However, causality between ICC preservation and improved gastric emptying was not established, and ICC pacemaker function was not assessed. Direct ICC protection by BXD serum and a causal role of PI3K/AKT/mTOR remain to be confirmed.

articles.title: Salidroside engages HSPA5 and attenuates PERK-eIF2α-ATF4-CHOP signalling in ovariectomy-induced bone loss.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Rhodiolae Crenulatae Radix et Rhizoma (Hong-jing-tian) is a well-documented traditional Chinese medicinal herb. Its pharmacopoeial marker salidroside exerts osteoprotective effects in ovariectomized models, yet its molecular targets remain elusive. AIM OF THE STUDY: To investigate salidroside-HSPA5 engagement, restoration of ER-stress-disrupted BiP-PERK association, and HSPA5 requirement for salidroside responses in stressed osteoblasts. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Ovariectomised rats received salidroside (30 or 100 mg·kg-1·d-1) or alendronate, followed by bone, serum and protein analyses. Plasma proteomics identified HSPA5. Salidroside-HSPA5 interaction was validated by docking, SPR, CETSA, DARTS and ATPase assays. Tunicamycin-stressed MC3T3-E1 osteoblasts were used to assess cellular rescue, HSPA5-PERK interaction (co-immunoprecipitation) and UPR signalling. Hspa5 siRNA verified HSPA5-dependent mechanisms. RESULTS: HSPA5 and eIF2α were core network nodes. Molecular docking predicted that salidroside binds to the HSPA5 ATPase domain (-8.53 kcal mol-1). Direct target engagement was supported by SPR (KD = 30.3 μM), CETSA (ΔTm = 2.61 °C) and DARTS assays, which showed concentration-dependent HSPA5 stabilization (90.0% residual HSPA5 at 1 mM salidroside vs. 38.3% for vehicle). Salidroside mildly suppressed recombinant HSPA5 ATPase activity (<30% inhibition at 1 mM). In ovariectomized rats, high-dose salidroside increased bone volume fraction from 9.8% to 36.4%, restored bone-formation markers and reduced ER-stress signalling. In tunicamycin-challenged osteoblasts, salidroside recovered viability, osteogenic differentiation and nuclear RUNX2. It attenuated three UPR branches and partially restored stress-disrupted HSPA5-PERK interaction (normalized co-precipitated HSPA5: 0.74 vs. 0.15, P = 0.001). Hspa5 knockdown abrogated the cytoprotective and osteogenic responses to salidroside. CONCLUSIONS: Salidroside engages HSPA5 to restore stress-disrupted BiP-PERK complexes. It suppresses pathological PERK-driven UPR over-activation and rescues osteoblast function in osteoporosis models. Its osteoprotection is HSPA5-dependent.

articles.title: Integrative network pharmacology, machine learning, and experimental validation identify the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 axis as a potential mechanism underlying the therapeutic effects of Lingguizhugan decoction in Alzheimer's disease.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Lingguizhugan decoction, a traditional formula originating from Zhang Zhongjing's Treatise on Cold Damage and Miscellaneous Diseases, has shown cognitive benefits in APP/PS1 mice in our earlier study, partly through restoration of meningeal lymphatic drainage and enhancement of amyloid-β (Aβ) removal. Whether other molecular events contribute to its therapeutic action in Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains to be clarified. AIM OF THE STUDY: This work was designed to clarify additional potential mechanisms by which LGZG may act against AD. METHODS AND MATERIALS: The chemical constituents of LGZG were profiled by UPLC-Q-TOF-MS. Candidate targets and pathways were screened by integrating public databases, transcriptomic analysis, network pharmacology, and enrichment analysis. Eight machine learning models and SHAP analysis were subsequently used to prioritize candidate regulators. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were performed to evaluate the potential interactions between representative LGZG constituents and TLR4. APP/PS1 mice and BV2 microglial cells were used for experimental validation. Spatial learning and memory, hippocampal pathological alterations, Aβ deposition, inflammatory cytokines, microglial inflammatory phenotype-associated markers, and TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 signaling were evaluated using behavioral testing, histological staining, ELISA, immunofluorescence, qRT-PCR, and Western blotting. TAK-242 inhibition and TLR4 overexpression were further used to assess the involvement of TLR4 signaling. RESULTS: Twenty-three candidate constituents were retained following chemical profiling and in silico screening of LGZG. Integrated analysis of network pharmacology, AD-related genes, and transcriptomic data identified 46 candidate LGZG-AD-DEG targets. Machine learning and SHAP analyses further prioritized several inflammation-related regulators, including RELA and NFKBIA, supporting inflammation-related signaling as a major direction for subsequent validation. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations suggested potential interactions between representative LGZG constituents and the TLR4 receptor. In APP/PS1 mice, LGZG improved spatial learning and memory, attenuated hippocampal neuronal injury, reduced Aβ deposition, and decreased IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α levels. LGZG also reduced hippocampal TLR4, P-IκBα, P-NF-κB, and NLRP3 expression and decreased TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3-related signals in Iba1-positive microglia. In LPS-stimulated BV2 cells, LGZG shifted inflammatory phenotype-associated markers toward a less pro-inflammatory profile and suppressed TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 signaling. TAK-242 treatment and TLR4 overexpression experiments further supported the involvement of TLR4 signaling in these effects. CONCLUSION: LGZG alleviated cognitive impairment, hippocampal pathological alterations, Aβ deposition, and neuroinflammatory responses in APP/PS1 mice. Integrated bioinformatic analyses and experimental validation suggest that regulation of TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 signaling contributes to the anti-neuroinflammatory effects of LGZG in AD.

articles.title: Integrated UPLC-Q-TOF and serum pharmacological analysis: Yinchenhao decoction alleviates alcoholic steatohepatitis via inhibition of COX-2/PI3K/Akt and suppression of M1 macrophage polarization.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Yinchenhao decoction (YCHD), a classic Traditional Chinese Medicine formula, has been widely used for the treatment of liver disorders. However, its therapeutic efficacy in alcoholic steatohepatitis (ASH) and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. AIM OF THE STUDY: To systematically evaluate the protective effects of YCHD and its bioactive compounds against ASH and elucidate the potential mechanisms through an integrated strategy combining UPLC-Q-TOF analysis and network pharmacology, with particular emphasis on the COX-2/PI3K/Akt signaling pathway and macrophage polarization. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The therapeutic effects of YCHD on lipid metabolism, oxidative stress, and inflammation were comprehensively evaluated using multiple experimental models. The chemical composition and material basis of YCHD were characterized by UPLC-Q-TOF analysis. Network pharmacology was subsequently employed to predict potential molecular targets and signaling pathways associated with the anti-ASH effects of YCHD. The regulatory effects of YCHD on macrophage polarization and the COX-2/PI3K/Akt signaling pathway were further investigated through COX-2 inhibitor celecoxib and COX-2 siRNA. Finally, the major active compounds were screened and experimentally validated in zebrafish, AML12 cells, and RAW264.7 cells. RESULTS: YCHD exerted protective effects across multiple experimental models by improving lipid metabolic disorders, reducing hepatic lipid accumulation, and alleviating inflammatory responses. Phytochemical profiling identified 1,740 compounds in YCHD, including 195 blood-absorbed components. Network pharmacology analysis suggested that the PI3K/Akt pathway represents a critical target underlying the therapeutic effects of YCHD. Further validation demonstrated that YCHD reduced the expression of macrophage M1 polarization markers CD80/CD86 and decreased the production of inflammatory cytokines in ASH mice. Consistently, YCHD serum exerted comparable protective effects in LPS-stimulated polarized RAW264.7 cells by suppressing the activation of the COX-2/PI3K/Akt signaling pathway. Pharmacological screening further identified acacetin, apigenin, and fisetin as potential key compounds. CONCLUSIONS: YCHD effectively ameliorates ASH by restoring lipid homeostasis, mitigating oxidative stress and inflammation, and suppressing M1 macrophage polarization through modulation of the COX-2/PI3K/Akt pathway. Acacetin, apigenin, and fisetin may represent important bioactive constituents contributing to the therapeutic effects of YCHD. These findings provide mechanistic insights into the pharmacological basis of YCHD in ASH treatment and establish a foundation for further identification and isolation of its active compounds.

articles.title: Impact of phosphate buffer strength and unbuffered water on ionizable drug powder dissolution.
articles.abstract: We are unaware of prior reports of the dependence of drug powder dissolution on buffer strength. The objective was to assess the effect of 5, 10, 50, and 100 mM sodium phosphate concentration on in vitro particle dissolution of ionizable drugs. Three weakly acidic drugs (naproxen, piroxicam, and phenytoin) and one weakly basic drug (dipyridamole) were studied at different pH conditions. Dissolution was conducted using USP Apparatus II with a mini-paddle at 37 °C in 100 mL media. Overall, the effect on dissolution profile was modest, with the largest effect generally being between 5 mM phosphate and zero phosphate (i.e., unbuffered water). Hence, a secondary objective was to predict the dissolution of the four ionizable drugs into unbuffered water, as well as for ibuprofen, ketoprofen, indomethacin, haloperidol, and meloxicam. Predictions anticipated slower ionizable drug dissolution into unbuffered water. Overall, dissolution predictions into buffer were better using the transient pH film model that accounts for the changing solid-liquid interfacial pH during dissolution, than for the conventional z-factor film model.

articles.title: Laser-responsive chitosan-coated solid lipid nanoparticles co-encapsulating CaO2 nanoparticles and IR780 for on-demand and enhanced photodynamic therapy of cancers.
articles.abstract: The photodynamic therapy (PDT) efficacy is limited by tumor hypoxia and inefficient intracellular accumulation of photosensitizers (PSs). This study reports chitosan-coated solid lipid nanoparticles (SLNs) co-encapsulating the near-infrared photosensitizer IR780 and oxygen-generating CaO2 nanoparticles (NPs) for on-demand and enhanced PDT. Under 808 nm laser irradiation, the resulting IRCa@SLN-CH nanoplatform undergoes phase change due to IR780 photothermal effects, triggering the release of IR780 and CaO2. The released CaO2 subsequently hydrolyzes to generate oxygen in situ, boosting singlet oxygen production by IR780. Successful chitosan coating was confirmed by FTIR spectroscopy and a zeta potential shift from -36.2 ± 3.6 mV (uncoated IRCa@SLN) to + 35.3 ± 6.6 mV (IRCa@SLN-CH). IRCa@SLN-CH exhibited an average particle size of 51.5 ± 19.3 nm by TEM and 77.6 ± 7.0 nm by DLS, with IR780 and CaO2 loadings of 4.23 ± 0.23% and 65 ± 7%, respectively. Dissolved oxygen (DO) and ROS measurements showed that chitosan coating improved payload protection, resulting in a more controlled, on-off activation profile in response to laser irradiation. In vitro tests using MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells demonstrated that chitosan coating enhanced cellular uptake, increased on-demand intracellular ROS generation, and improved laser-responsive cytotoxicity, while maintaining low ROS generation and toxicity before laser activation. Cell viability remained high before irradiation (99 ± 1%) but reduced to 51 ± 3% following laser exposure. Overall, the IRCa@SLN-CH nanoplatform shows potential for on-demand and enhanced PDT.

articles.title: From particle engineering to direct compression: Tailoring compaction properties through microfluidic API-excipient co-processing.
articles.abstract: Direct compression (DC) is an attractive route for tablet manufacturing, yet its impact remains constrained by the poor flowability of many active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and the high excipient loading required for reliable compaction. Here, we introduce a microfluidic particle engineering approach that co-processes API with polymeric excipients to produce highly flowable microparticles with tuneable compaction behaviour. Notably, excellent tabletability is achieved with minimal excipient loading, thereby addressing both critical requirements of DC. Using a parallelized step-emulsification device, monodispersed droplets containing dissolved naproxen (NPX) and ethyl cellulose (EC) were fabricated and subjected to antisolvent extraction to produce spherical co-processed microparticles. Robust tablet tensile strength exceeding 5 MPa was achieved with only 11% excipient loading - enabled by a self-assembled core-shell structure featuring an EC-rich shell encapsulating an NPX-rich core. Moreover, adjusting the API-to-excipient ratio produced microparticles with distinct morphologies and solid-state outcomes, resulting in greater tabletability with higher excipient loading. Overall, the microfluidic platform approach allows for a systematic study of self-assembled particle structures produced by API-excipient co-processing and their impact on DC formulations.

articles.title: Validating complete-airway computational fluid dynamics (CA-CFD) predictions of regional aerosol deposition in human subjects: comparisons with in vivo data of pharmaceutical aerosol delivery during HFNC therapy.
articles.abstract: High-Flow Nasal Cannula (HFNC) is a critical tool for respiratory support in acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and for subjects with general hypoxemia; however, pharmaceutical aerosol delivery simultaneous with HFNC support is known to be highly inefficient. The aim of this study was to develop and validate a high-fidelity, complete-airway computational fluid dynamics (CA-CFD) model of regional aerosol deposition that occurs when a pharmaceutical aerosol product is administered through a nasal interface simultaneously with HFNC therapy. The CFD model included the aerosol delivery tubing and interface connected to a complete-airway (CA) model extending from the extrathoracic nose-throat (NT) region through the conducting airways and alveoli. CFD-predicted regional aerosol deposition was compared with previously published in vivo experimental data. Predictions of the CA-CFD model agreed closely with the available cohort-level human-subject in vivo data including a predicted aerosol deposition fraction in the lungs of 2.9% (based on nebulized dose) compared with in vivo medians of 2.1% (gamma scintigraphy; range: 1.5-2.9%) and 3.7% (SPECT-CT; range: 2.2-4.7%). In addition to low lung delivery efficiency, the regional drug delivery showed high heterogeneity. Considering a map of regional airway deposition, utilizing a realistic polydisperse droplet size distribution in the stochastic individual path (SIP) models, deposition fractions in the NT, upper tracheobronchial (TB), middle TB, lower TB and alveolar regions were 16%, 0.5%, 0.1%, 0.1%, and 2.4% of the nebulized dose, with ∼ 22% of the nebulized dose exhaled/escaped/dripped, while ∼ 58% was lost in the HFNC circuit. Through methodical development, a CA-CFD model of aerosol delivery during HFNC therapy was established that closely agrees with the in vivo cohort-level data and can now serve as a "representative population-level digital twin" to optimize aerosol delivery during this highly challenging but clinically popular mode of ventilation support.

articles.title: Redispersible triclabendazole nanocrystals with enhanced dissolution and in vitro mucin interaction.
articles.abstract: Fascioliasis is a neglected tropical disease caused by the parasitic flatworms Fasciola hepatica and Fasciola gigantica. Triclabendazole (TCBZ) is the first-line treatment; however, its poor aqueous solubility and high lipophilicity limit its dissolution in gastrointestinal fluids, which may compromise oral performance. TCBZ can be considered a BCS Class II or BCS II-like compound, since its biopharmaceutical behavior is mainly limited by low aqueous solubility and dissolution rate. In this study, TCBZ nanocrystals (TCBZ-NCs) were produced by microsphere-assisted nanomilling and subsequently converted into a redispersible powder by spray drying. The resulting formulation displayed an average hydrodynamic diameter of approximately 355 nm after redispersion, a polydispersity index of approximately 0.3, a zeta potential of approximately - 24 mV, and colloidal stability for up to 90 days at room temperature. SEM and STEM analyses supported the formation of nanosized particles, while FTIR and XRPD analyses indicated no detectable chemical modification and preservation of the crystalline state after processing. TCBZ-NCs exhibited markedly improved dissolution compared with raw TCBZ under acidic non-sink and sink conditions, and retained a clear advantage in phosphate buffer at pH 6.8. In addition, mucin interaction studies and in vitro detachment-force measurements using hydrated model surfaces suggested in vitro mucin-interaction potential. Overall, these results support TCBZ-NCs as a high-drug-load crystalline formulation strategy for improving the dissolution behavior of TCBZ. Further studies using biorelevant dissolution media, cellular, ex vivo, and in vivo models are required to determine whether these in vitro findings translate into improved oral absorption or therapeutic performance.

articles.title: Inhibition of neutrophil extracellular trap formation ameliorates astrocyte pyroptosis via CUL7-dependent NLRP3 ubiquitination in mice with sepsis-associated encephalopathy.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) encompasses acute brain dysfunction during sepsis and may be followed by persistent cognitive impairment among survivors. Although neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) have been implicated in sepsis-related organ injury, their role in astrocyte fate determination and neuroinflammation during SAE remains poorly defined. Here, using a cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) model, we demonstrate that NETs accumulate in both the circulation and hippocampus following sepsis. Pharmacological inhibition or degradation of NETs markedly alleviated blood-brain barrier disruption, neuroinflammation, neuronal death, and acute neurobehavioral abnormalities. Mechanistically, NET accumulation was associated with enhanced astrocyte pyroptosis via activation of the NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3)-caspase-1-gasdermin D (GSDMD) pathway. Activation of NLRP3 abolished the neuroprotective effects conferred by NET inhibition. Transcriptomic analysis of human hippocampal tissues identified cullin 7 (CUL7) as a sepsis-associated candidate, and subsequent experiments showed that its expression was restored following NET inhibition. CUL7 physically interacted with NLRP3, enhanced its ubiquitination, and reduced its protein stability, thereby restraining astrocyte pyroptosis. Notably, CUL7 overexpression improved acute neurobehavioral outcomes, preserved blood-brain barrier integrity, and attenuated neuroinflammation in septic mice. Collectively, our findings identify a previously unrecognized NETs-CUL7-NLRP3 axis that governs astrocyte pyroptosis and contributes to the pathogenesis of SAE, highlighting CUL7 as a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: Melatonin ameliorates anxiety-like behavior and intestinal barrier dysfunction induced by high-fat diet in BTBR mice.
Hyperoside promotes ferroptosis in prostate cancer by modulation of tryptophan metabolism via flotillin-2 reduction.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hyperoside (HYP), a flavonoid derived from Hypericum perforatum, has been demonstrated to effectively inhibit prostate cancer (PCa) both in vitro and in vivo. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying this effect remain to be elucidated. AIM: To investigate the specific mechanisms by which HYP exerts its anti-PCa effects. METHODS: We identified HYP targets using small-molecule target prediction and molecular docking, validated by Western blotting, the cellular thermal shift assay and Microscale thermophoresis (MST). Downstream signaling was explored via RNA sequencing, Western blotting, and reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). Tryptophan (TRP) metabolism was assessed by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay and Western blotting, whereas ferroptosis was evaluated by gene set enrichment analysis, biochemical assays, reactive oxygen species (ROS) measurement, and Western blotting. Rescue experiments using RO8191 and kynurenine (KYN), together with in vivo xenograft models, were used for validation. RESULTS: HYP interacted with flotillin-2 (FLOT2), downregulating its expression, thereby inhibiting Signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) and Indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1 (IDO1) expression, blocking the conversion of TRP to KYN, and weakening KYN-aryl hydrocarbon receptor feedback. HYP upregulated ACSL4 and downregulated glutathione peroxidase 4 and SLC7A11, resulting in lipid peroxidation, ROS accumulation, iron overload, and glutathione depletion. RO8191 or KYN reversed these effects. In vivo, HYP suppressed tumor growth, disrupted TRP metabolism, and induced ferroptosis. CONCLUSION: By interacting with FLOT2 and suppressing the STAT3/IDO1/TRP metabolism axis, HYP induces ferroptosis in PCa, thereby identifying a novel therapeutic axis for PCa and supporting the potential of HYP as a promising natural therapeutic candidate.

articles.title: Stigmasterol Ameliorates Pulmonary Hypertension by Suppressing the CCL5/CCR5 Signaling Pathway: Taurocholic Acid as a Downstream Mediator.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a devastating disease characterized by irreversible pulmonary vascular remodeling (PVR), ultimately culminating in right ventricular failure and death. Although previous studies have demonstrated that stigmasterol (STG) reduces cholesterol levels and prevents cardiovascular diseases, its potential role in PH remains unknown. In this study, we investigated the therapeutic effects of STG on SU5416/hypoxia (Su/Hx)-induced PH in mice and elucidated the underlying molecular mechanisms. METHODS: Through bioinformatics analysis and network pharmacology, we identified STG as a promising herbal compound for PH treatment. Both in vitro and in vivo experiments validated that STG ameliorates platelet-derived growth factor-BB (PDGF-BB)-induced proliferation and migration of pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (PASMCs), as well as PVR and right ventricular hypertrophy (RVH). Molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, MM-PBSA calculation, and microscale thermophoresis (MST) were used to validate direct STG-CCL5 binding. Functional rescue experiments with taurocholic acid (TCA) were also performed. RESULTS: Molecular docking, MD simulation, and MST revealed spontaneous direct binding between CCL5 and STG, with an MST-derived KD of 4.72 μM. While CCL5 promoted PDGF-BB-induced PASMC proliferation and migration, CCR5 inhibition counteracted these effects. STG ameliorated PASMC proliferation and migration by modulating CCL5. Furthermore, metabolomics and mass spectrometry analyses showed decreased taurocholic acid levels in lung tissues of CCR5-knockout (CCR5-/-) mice in the Su/Hx model. TCA reversed the protective effects of STG on PASMC proliferation and migration, supporting TCA as a downstream functional mediator. CONCLUSION: In conclusion, our study demonstrates that STG ameliorates Su/Hx-induced PH by modulating the CCL5/CCR5 signaling pathway, with taurocholic acid acting as a downstream mediator. Further investigations are warranted to explore the clinical applicability of STG-based therapies for PH patients.

articles.title: Calycosin-7-O-β-D-glucoside alleviates neurological injury after traumatic brain injury: involvement of cGAS-STING signaling and mitochondrial dynamics.
articles.abstract: Secondary neurological injury is a major determinant of functional outcome after traumatic brain injury (TBI) and is closely linked to mitochondrial dysfunction and disrupted mitochondrial dynamics. Calycosin-7-O-β-D-glucoside (CAG) has antioxidant and mitochondria-protective properties, but its therapeutic potential in TBI remains unclear. The present study demonstrated that CAG significantly improved neurological, behavioral, and cognitive outcomes in mice with controlled cortical impact (CCI)-induced TBI, while alleviating histopathological damage, neuronal apoptosis, glial activation, and mitochondrial ultrastructural abnormalities. Consistently, in H2O2-treated HT22 cells, CAG reduced oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and apoptosis. Mechanistically, transcriptomic, protein, and confocal immunofluorescence analyses showed that CAG reduced aberrant cGAS-STING signaling and attenuated abnormal subcellular redistribution of activated STING. In parallel, CAG restored mitochondrial dynamics, with a reduced p-DRP1 (Ser616)/DRP1 ratio and increased MFN1, MFN2, and OPA1 expression. Notably, DMXAA partially reversed CAG-mediated restoration of mitochondrial dynamics and neuroprotection, suggesting the involvement of STING signaling. CAG promotes neurological recovery after TBI by restoring mitochondrial dynamics homeostasis and attenuating neuronal injury, with the findings supporting the involvement of reduced cGAS-STING signaling in these effects. This study provides experimental evidence supporting CAG as a potential pharmacological strategy for mitigating secondary injury after TBI.

articles.title: Liquid ingress or matrix strength? Using magnesium stearate lubrication to distinguish tablet disintegration factors in MCC and lactose tablets.
articles.abstract: Tablet disintegration results from a competition between liquid penetration and subsequent disintegration-promoting mechanisms on one hand, and mechanical resistance of the tablet matrix on the other, but their relative contributions are difficult to separate experimentally. Here, magnesium stearate (MgSt) lubrication was used to distinguish these effects in microcrystalline cellulose (MCC) and α-lactose monohydrate (lactose) tablets, characterised by terahertz pulsed imaging to monitor liquid ingress kinetics and tensile strength testing. Increasing MgSt concentration slowed liquid ingress in both matrices, but disintegration times diverged. MCC disintegration was governed primarily by matrix resistance and was therefore accelerated by MgSt-induced weakening of the matrix. In contrast, lactose disintegration was governed primarily by liquid ingress kinetics and was consequently slowed by MgSt, as conventionally expected. Notably, the effect of porosity on disintegration times could be attributed to the same mechanistic principles in the two systems. The results indicate that matrix strength, not only liquid ingress, can be a dominant factor controlling disintegration kinetics. Overall, the findings support incorporating matrix strength as a distinct factor in disintegration testing and formulation design, with MgSt lubrication providing a useful strategy for identifying systems in which matrix resistance dominates disintegration.

articles.title: Construction of a mitotane delivery system based on γ-cyclodextrin metal organic framework and its enhanced anti-tumor activity.
articles.abstract: Adrenocortical carcinoma (ACC) is an aggressive cancer with an urgent need for more effective and safer therapies. Mitotane (MT), has its clinical utility compromised by poor aqueous solubility and low oral bioavailability. In response, a novel nano-delivery platform was fabricated by encapsulating MT into γ-cyclodextrin metal-organic framework (γ-CD-MOF), denoted as MT@γ-CD-MOF. The composite was prepared via a solvothermal method. Comprehensive characterization combined with molecular simulation confirmed the successful loading of MT in a molecularly dispersed state within the γ-CD cavities, with a drug loading capacity of 20.04% and an approximately 3.8-fold increase in apparent solubility. In vitro studies demonstrated that MT@γ-CD-MOF suppressed the proliferation and migration of SW-13 ACC and enhanced pro-apoptotic effects by activating Caspase-3 and increasing intracellular reactive oxygen species levels. Importantly, in vivo pharmacokinetic studies in rats revealed a substantial improvement in oral bioavailability, with the area under the concentration-time curve from 0 to 24 h (AUC0-24 h) increasing by 1.71-fold compared with raw MT. These results indicate that MT@γ-CD-MOF is an efficient and biocompatible oral delivery platform, offering a promising formulation strategy to enhance the therapeutic efficacy of MT against ACC.

articles.title: Label-free protein quantification in complex formulations using intrinsic fluorescence gel electrophoresis.
articles.abstract: This study establishes a gel electrophoresis-based intrinsic fluorescence imaging (GE-IFI) method for dye-free detection of protein samples in complex buffer systems. The method utilizes the intrinsic fluorescence of proteins, primarily from tryptophan residues, as the signal source, avoiding the system dependence of extrinsic colorimetric reactions. The method was tested under conditions simulating critical steps in bioprocessing-denaturation (high urea), protein purification (weak acid), and high-salt formulation-using Denosumab and BSA to challenge its robustness. It exhibited stable signals across diverse systems and showed comparable or improved analytical robustness compared with conventional colorimetric methods under the evaluated conditions. The quantitative accuracy of GE-IFI was further validated by SEC-HPLC under acidic formulation conditions, demonstrating excellent agreement between fluorescence-based and chromatographic quantification. Based on the detection of intrinsic protein fluorescence, GE-IFI enables quantitative protein detection with reduced susceptibility to matrix effects from complex chemical environments. The method maintains high linearity and reproducibility across different formulation systems, offering a potential analytical strategy for monitoring protein concentration changes and aggregation-related molecular states during biopharmaceutical development.

articles.title: Optimizing pediatric melatonin therapy through semi solid extrusion of tailored dosage forms.
articles.abstract: Pediatric drug therapy lacks suitable individualized dosage forms, and semi-solid extrusion (SSE) is a promising compounding technology for producing patient-specific formulations. Melatonin was formulated in three dosage forms: CuraBlend® gel tablets (1% and 2.5% w/w), anhydrous troches (1% w/w) and orodispersible films (ODFs; 0.25% w/w). Each dosage form was produced in various sizes, giving target doses of 0.81-12.5 mg. The formulations were evaluated for content uniformity, 3-month stability and in vitro dissolution, and their solid state was characterized by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC). All printed tablets, and ODFs met pharmacopoeia requirements for mass and content uniformity, and stable assay results over three months. ODFs showed almost 100% release within 3 minutes. Melatonin formulations achieved over 70-90% drug release within 60 minutes depending on PS80 concentration, and the 2.5% melatonin formulations exceeded 90% release. 1% of melatonin in troche demonstrated complete drug release within 10 minutes. DSC showed that melatonin's melting peak at 117°C was absent in most formulations, suggesting dissolution of the drug in the excipient bases. SSE compounding platform enables the accurate, reproducible compounding of pediatric melatonin dosage forms in both development and hospital settings.

articles.title: Involvement of PINK1-related Mitophagy and Necroptosis in TDI-Induced Experimental Asthma.
articles.abstract: Toluene diisocyanate (TDI) is a prevalent cause of occupational asthma. Although mitophagy contributes to various pulmonary diseases, its role and downstream signaling in TDI-induced asthma remain unclear. In this study, we first utilized BALB/c mice to investigate the effects of TDI exposure on pulmonary injury, mitophagy, and associated regulatory mechanisms. Based on these findings, we constructed an adverse outcome pathway (AOP) network for TDI-induced asthma. Mechanistic connections predicted by the AOP were validated in vitro using PINK1-knockdown bronchial epithelial cells, assessing PINK1-related mitophagy, mitochondrial function, cytosolic mtDNA release, attenuated the increased expression of cGAS/STING pathway-related proteins, and necroptosis. Finally, we predicted potential natural product therapeutics through bioactivity screening and toxicity profiling, targeting key genes implicated in TDI-induced asthma. Integration of in vivo, in vitro, and AOP network analyses indicated that TDI exposure induced airway hyperresponsiveness and pulmonary histopathological changes, along with elevated Th2 cytokine production. This exposure selectively upregulated PINK1 and Parkin expression, without altering levels of BNIP3, NIX, or FUNDC1. PINK1 knockdown mitigated TDI-induced mitophagy-related alterations, restored mitochondrial function, reduced cytosolic mtDNA release, attenuated the increased expression of cGAS/STING pathway-related proteins, and reduced necroptosis. In silico screening predicted β-lapachone, genistein, and apigenin as promising candidate therapeutics for TDI-induced asthma. Overall, PINK1-related mitophagy may contribute to TDI-induced occupational asthma, and natural compounds identified via in silico screening are potential candidates that require further in vitro and in vivo validation of their safety and efficacy.

articles.title: Chronic Neurotoxicity of Di-2-ethylhexyl phthalate (DEHP) at no observed adverse effects level (NOAEL) doses on adult zebrafish links to Neuro-behavioral disorder.
articles.abstract: Di-2-ethylhexyl phthalate (DEHP), as the most common member of phthalic acid esters (PAEs), is considered an endocrine-disrupting compound (EDC) and causes prominent developmental, reproductive toxicity, metabolic dysfunctions, and neurotoxicity. However, the potential neurotoxicity associated with chronic DEHP exposure at concentrations below the no-observed-adverse-effect level (NOAEL) in adult zebrafish remains poorly understood, largely due to a lack of experimental evidence from animal studies. Thus, to comprehensively characterize the potential neurological effects of DEHP, adult zebrafish were used as an animal model to evaluate neurotoxicity following 4 weeks of exposure to DEHP at concentrations within the NOAEL range (5, 50, and 200 mg/L). Behavioral assessments included the light-dark preference test, novel tank diving test, novel object exploration test, social interactions test, and conditioned place preference (CPP) test. After 4 weeks of chronic exposure to DEHP, zebrafish exhibited marked neurobehavioral alterations, including increased time spent and distance traveled in the dark zone and reduced exploratory behavior in unfamiliar environments (reduced exploration of the top zone in the novel tank and of the novel object zone); DEHP exposure also disrupted social interactions and impaired learning and memory in zebrafish. The LC-MS/MS results revealed that changes in neuro-behavioral profiles were closely associated with neurotransmitter levels in the brain of zebrafish. The present study provides a valuable reference for drawing attention to the assessment of DEHP neurotoxicity under the NOAEL.

articles.title: DHA-H and HPA restore impaired neurogenic phenotypes and BDNF-TrkB signaling in Ts65Dn neurospheres and hippocampus.
articles.abstract: Impaired neurogenesis is a hallmark of neurodevelopmental disorders, including Down syndrome, and contributes to long-lasting deficits in brain structure and function. Membrane lipid composition is emerging as a critical regulator of cell fate decisions in the developing and adult brain. Here we investigate the pro-neurogenic potential of the synthetic PUFA DHA-H (2-hydroxylated DHA) and its immediate metabolite HPA (Heneicosapentaenoic acid) in cellular and tissue models derived from the Ts65Dn mouse model of Down syndrome, using DHA (docosahexaenoic acid) as a reference pro-neurogenic ω-3 PUFA. In primary neurospheres, DHA-H and HPA increased the expression of neural stem and progenitor cell markers, including Sox2, Ki67, and Nestin, and stimulated proliferative activity, accompanied by a parallel upregulation of early neuronal differentiation markers such as Doublecortin and PSA-NCAM. Notably, both compounds promoted the recovery of these markers in Ts65Dn neurospheres, with HPA achieving restoration to wild-type levels for several markers, while DHA-H exerted beneficial effects that varied across the evaluated parameters. These improvements were associated with enhanced BDNF production and TrkB phosphorylation, highlighting the BDNF-TrkB signaling axis as a potential molecular mediator of their pro-neurogenic effects. In vivo, administration of DHA-H and HPA increased BDNF and phospho-TrkB protein levels, together with the number of proliferating cells and mature neurons in the dentate gyrus of the hippocampus, suggesting enhanced activity of the adult neurogenic niche and potential neuroprotective effects. Together, our findings identify DHA-H and HPA as promising modulators of neural progenitor dynamics and neurogenesis in a trisomic context, revealing a lipid-dependent mechanism of neurodevelopmental plasticity and supporting their therapeutic potential for ameliorating impaired neurogenic programs in Down syndrome and related disorders.

articles.title: Lipid-based nanoencapsulation prolongs the antinociceptive effect of cannabidiol in experimental neuropathic pain.
articles.abstract: Neuropathic pain (NP) is a debilitating chronic condition frequently refractory to available therapies, while the therapeutic potential of cannabidiol (CBD) is limited by its unfavorable physicochemical and pharmacokinetic properties. This study investigated whether incorporation of CBD into a lipid-based microemulsion (LS-CBD) could improve its antinociceptive profile in a murine model of NP, and explored potential molecular mechanisms and safety. LS-CBD was prepared by a high-energy emulsification method and exhibited nanometric droplet size, narrow size distribution, high entrapment efficiency (96.8 ± 0.7%), and physicochemical stability over 60 days. Male C57BL/6 mice subjected to partial sciatic nerve ligation were evaluated for mechanical and thermal nociception following acute and repeated oral administration of CBD and LS-CBD (25, 50, and 75 mg/kg). Compared with free CBD, LS-CBD prolonged the duration of thermal antinociception (1-8 h vs. 2 h) and produced a significantly greater global antinociceptive effect. Peak antinociception did not differ between formulations (50.0 ± 14.9% vs. 53.2 ± 25.5%), indicating that nanoencapsulation prolonged the response rather than increasing its magnitude. Under repeated administration, LS-CBD produced significant mechanical antinociceptive activity on every day of the seven-day treatment period, while both formulations produced comparable and sustained thermal antinociception without evidence of tolerance development. At the molecular level, both CBD and LS-CBD increased Sod1 and Cat transcripts relative to naive animals, and reduced Nos2 and Gfap transcripts relative to neuropathic controls, in the dorsal root ganglia, suggesting attenuation of nitrosative stress and satellite glial cell activation. Neither treatment induced hematological, biochemical, or body weight alterations following repeated administration. These findings support lipid-based nanoencapsulation as a strategy to extend the duration of CBD antinociception after oral administration.

articles.title: Neuromodulatory properties of thiopyrano[2,3-d]thiazole Les-2769: In silico and in vitro γ-aminobutryic acid/glutamatergic neurotransmission studies.
articles.abstract: Nitrogen- and sulfur-containing heterocycles represent key chemotypes in the design of central nervous system-active agents, including potential modulators of γ-aminobutryic acid (GABA)ergic homeostasis. Among them, thiopyrano[2,3-d]thiazoles have recently attracted attention because of their ability to influence GABA-related pathways. In this study, we investigated the in silico molecular docking and presynaptic neuropharmacological effects of the thiopyrano[2,3-d]thiazole derivative Les-2769. Functional studies using isolated presynaptic rat cortical nerve terminals (synaptosomes) demonstrated that Les-2769 dose-dependently inhibited transporter-mediated [3H]GABA uptake and accumulation and increased extrasynaptosomal [3H]GABA levels. At 10 μM, Les-2769 increased synaptosomal uptake of L-[14C]glutamate, indicating an opposite regulation of GABAergic and glutamatergic transport processes. Membrane depolarization-induced reversal of GABA and glutamate transporters was not affected by Les-2769. The compound significantly increased spontaneous [3H]GABA release in the presence of the GABA transporter inhibitor 1,2,5,6-tetrahydro-1-(2-(((diphenylmethylene)amino)oxy)ethyl)-3-pyridinecarboxylic acid hydrochloride, whereas the GABAA receptor antagonist flumazenil failed to modify this effect, excluding the involvement of GABAA receptor signaling. Fluorimetric analysis of synaptic vesicle acidification and membrane potential corroborated the radiolabeled uptake and release data. Collectively, Les-2769 exhibits an uncommon and pharmacologically valuable presynaptic profile, characterized by low-micromolar bidirectional modulation of GABAergic and glutamatergic neurotransmission. This functional asymmetry could suggest potential anticonvulsant, antidepressant, anxiolytic, antipsychotic, hypnotic, and anti-post-traumatic stress response/disorder properties within a defined concentration window. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: The present study identified Les-2769 as a 4-thiazolidinone derivative with a rare and pharmacologically valuable presynaptic profile. Its ability at low micromolar concentrations to oppositely regulate GABA-ergic and glutamatergic transport processes distinguished it from classical GABA uptake inhibitors and supported further investigation of this compound class as potential anticonvulsant, anxiolytic, antidepressant, and anti-post-traumatic stress response/disorder agents, provided that dosing remained within the mechanistic window that preserved this functional asymmetry.

articles.title: Bioactivatable conjugated nanocarriers for synergistic mRNA-mediated cancer immunotherapy.
articles.abstract: mRNA immunotherapy holds transformative potential in oncology, yet single-agent approaches frequently fail against immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments (TMEs). Bioactivatable co-delivery of immunogenic chemotherapy alongside mRNA offers mechanistically synergistic advantages, yet coformulation of hydrophobic small-molecule prodrugs with hydrophilic mRNA in a single stable nanoparticle remains a major unresolved engineering challenge. We synthesized an activatable lipid-prodrug by covalently tethering an hydrogen peroxide-responsive thioketal-oxaliplatin conjugate to dilinoleylmethyl-4-dimethylaminobutyrate via amide coupling, and formulated bioactivatable conjugated nanocarriers (BCNs) by microfluidic nanoprecipitation. Four formulations were comprehensively characterized and evaluated for mRNA expression, cellular uptake, endosomal escape, immune activation, cytotoxicity, and in vivo antitumor efficacy, TME remodeling, immune memory, and systemic safety. BCN-D (combination) exhibited a hydrodynamic diameter of 112 ± 3.5 nm (polydispersity index = 0.09), mRNA encapsulation efficiency of 91.5% ± 1.6%, reactive oxygen species -triggered drug release of 88% in tumor homogenate versus <12% in PBS, and 60-day colloidal stability. BCN-D was associated with increased expression of cGAS- stimulator of interferon genes pathway markers and prominent ICD hallmarks (calreticulin: 7.8-fold; HMGB1: 7.1-fold), Th1-skewed cytokine secretion (IFN-γ: 8.9-fold; IL-2: 11.3-fold), and a selectivity index (SI) >100 vs normal cells. In the B16-F10 syngeneic model, BCN-D achieved 84.7% tumor growth inhibition (combination index = 0.62), significantly prolonged survival (median not reached at day 40), and 100% durable tumor rejection upon rechallenge in complete responders. Tumor-infiltrating CD8+/Treg ratio improved 23-fold versus vehicle. Together, these findings characterize BCN-D as a combination nanocarrier in this preclinical model, with observed associations among ROS-responsive prodrug release, immune-marker changes, TME remodeling, and antitumor activity. These findings support further mechanistic investigation and evaluation in additional preclinical models before conclusions regarding translational applicability can be drawn. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This study presents bioactivatable conjugated nanocarriers combining reactive oxygen species-responsive oxaliplatin prodrug activation with mRNA immunotherapy, associated with altered tumor immune composition and antitumor activity in tested models. Building on prodrug-tethered ionizable lipid nanoparticles, it provides an incremental extension through thioketal-phenylboronic acid linker chemistry, an oxaliplatin prodrug designed to induce immunogenic cell death, and evaluation in melanoma. Translational relevance requires validation in additional preclinical systems.

articles.title: TAILORing ibrutinib dose and plasma levels in the real-life patient with chronic lymphocytic leukemia.
articles.abstract: Ibrutinib is the cornerstone of treatment of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL); however, cardiovascular adverse events (AE) may limit its long-term use. We performed a prospective, multicenter, real-life study that investigated the relationships between ibrutinib steady-state trough plasma concentrations (Cmin), the risk of development of AE, and the effects of dose reduction. Forty-eight patients with CLL treated with 420 mg/day ibrutinib were enrolled. Thirteen patients developed AE and exhibited significantly higher Cmin (geometric mean of 18.3 ng/mL) than patients without AE (geometric mean of 2.6 ng/mL, P < .0001). Logistic regression analyses showed that age and ibrutinib plasma levels were independent predictors of AE. Following temporary ibrutinib discontinuation, leading to resolution or mitigation of AE, ibrutinib was resumed at 280 mg/day, which lowered Cmin to a geometric mean of 3.4 ng/mL, similar to the Cmin measured in patients without AE. Adverse events did not recur in patients managed by DR. These real-life data show that dose reduction helps to normalize ibrutinib plasma exposure in CLL patients at risk of AE. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: In patients with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) treated with the Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitor ibrutinib, development of cardiovascular adverse events (AE) seems to associate with increased ibrutinib plasma levels compared with patients without AE. Dose reduction from 420 to 280 mg/day effectively reduces ibrutinib plasma levels and helps to resolve or mitigate AE. These findings call for reconsidering the ibrutinib dose in CLL patients and provide clinical pharmacology evidence that individualized dose reduction may improve the therapeutic index of ibrutinib.

articles.title: Trigonelline attenuates thioacetamide-induced nephrotoxicity through modulation of KIM-1/NGAL expression, and suppression of oxidative stress, renal apoptosis, inflammation, and fibrosis.
articles.abstract: Trigonelline (TRG) is a naturally occurring pyridine alkaloid that was first isolated from fenugreek seed. It is traditionally used for its hypoglycemic, hypolipidemic and neuroprotective properties. It has antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-apoptotic properties. Thioacetamide (TAA) is a well-established chemical that causes hepatotoxicity and also causes renal injury, characterised by oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis, and structural and functional kidney damage. Thus, TAA-induced nephrotoxicity serves as a useful experimental model for elucidating the mechanisms underlying chemically induced renal injury and for evaluating potential nephroprotective agents. This study investigated the nephroprotective potential of TRG against TAA-induced renal injury. We used network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamic simulation and an experimental approach to support our research findings. Network pharmacology identified Nuclear Factor Kappa B Subunit 1 (NF-κB1), Matrix Metalloproteinase - 9 (MMP-9), and Nuclear Factor Erythroid 2-Related Factor 2 (Nrf2) as potential targets, which were further supported through molecular docking studies and molecular dynamic simulation. Experimental nephrotoxicity was induced in rats by TAA at a dosage of 200 mg/kg via the i.p. route every third day for 8 weeks. TRG co-treatment was administered at doses of 20 and 40 mg/kg via the p.o. route every day for 8 weeks. After completion of treatment, biochemical, histopathological, and gene expression analyses were performed. TRG significantly reduces the increased levels of serum creatinine, blood urea nitrogen, malondialdehyde, and nitrite levels, while significantly increasing superoxide dismutase. Moreover, TRG significantly improved TAA-induced histopathological abnormalities by attenuating glomerular morphology, reducing tubular degeneration, and decreasing collagen accumulation in kidney tissues. At the molecular level, TRG treatment attenuated TAA-induced renal injury by downregulating the expression of Kidney Injury Molecule - 1 (KIM-1), Neutrophil Gelatinase-Associated Lipocalin (NGAL), NF-κB, Tumour Necrosis Factor-Alpha (TNF-α), Caspase - 3, Transforming Growth Factor-Beta (TGF-β), and MMP-9. Further, TRG upregulated the expression of B-cell Lymphoma 2 (Bcl-2) and modulated the compensatory upregulation of the Nrf2/HO-1 pathway. The study findings showed that TRG attenuated TAA-induced nephrotoxicity by restoring antioxidant defences, reducing renal injury biomarkers, suppressing inflammation, apoptosis, and fibrosis, and improving renal histopathological alterations. These findings highlight the potential of TRG as a promising natural nephroprotective agent against chemically induced kidney injury.

articles.title: Astragaloside IV ameliorates combined allergic rhinitis and asthma syndrome by inhibiting the activation of the STAT6/GATA3/IL-4 and PI3K/AKT/NF-κB signaling pathways.
articles.abstract: Astragaloside IV (As-IV) has demonstrated therapeutic potential for allergic rhinitis and asthma. However, a systematic investigation is lacking. This study was aimed at systematically elucidating the molecular mechanisms of As-IV in treating combined allergic rhinitis and asthma syndrome (CARAS) through network pharmacology combined with RNA sequencing analysis. A BALB/c mouse model of CARAS was established using ovalbumin. Nasal and bronchopulmonary allergic symptoms were recorded. Histopathological changes in the respiratory tract were assessed via H&E, PAS, and Masson staining. Network pharmacology and lung RNA sequencing were systematically employed to predict potential molecular mechanisms. WB, IF, and IHC were used to validate the activation of the STAT6/GATA3/IL-4 and PI3K/AKT/NF-κB signaling pathways, as well as the expression of epithelial barrier and mesenchymal components. Finally, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were performed to evaluate the binding affinity of As-IV with key target proteins. As-IV alleviated allergic symptoms, improved histopathological morphology, and reduced eosinophil and Th2 cell infiltration. Furthermore, As-IV markedly suppressed the activation of STAT6/GATA3/IL-4 and PI3K/AKT/NF-κB signaling pathways, mitigated epithelial barrier damage, and decreased mesenchymal component expression. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations confirmed that As-IV may potentially interact with STAT6 and AKT, suggesting its ability to modulate their conformations and biological activities. As-IV attenuates type 2 inflammation and epithelial barrier injury in the respiratory tract by inhibiting the STAT6/GATA3/IL-4 and PI3K/AKT/NF-κB signaling pathways. This study is the first to systematically unravel and validate the molecular mechanisms of As-IV in CARAS through integrated network pharmacology and RNA sequencing analysis, providing a robust scientific basis for its therapeutic application.

articles.title: Melatonin attenuates acute kidney injury in rats: modulation of the p53-PUMA/Bcl-2-Bax apoptotic signaling axis.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is characterized by oxidative stress-mediated tubular damage and activation of apoptosis-related signaling pathways. This study aimed to investigate the potential protective effect of melatonin on renal injury, focusing on histopathological alterations, apoptosis-related gene expression, and renal function parameters in an experimental AKI model. Twenty-eight rats were randomly assigned to four groups: Control, AKI, AKI + Solvent (1% ethanol), and AKI + Melatonin (20 mg/kg, intraperitoneal). AKI was induced by 45 min of renal ischemia followed by 24 h of reperfusion. At the end of the experimental period, kidney tissues were collected for histopathological evaluation using hematoxylin-eosin (H&E) and periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) staining. Apoptosis-related proteins (p53, PUMA, NOXA, Bax, and Bcl-2) were analyzed by immunofluorescence, and the expression levels of the corresponding genes were quantified using real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR). Renal function was assessed by measuring serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen (BUN) levels. AKI induced marked histopathological damage compared with the Control group (p < 0.001), whereas melatonin treatment significantly attenuated tissue injury. Immunofluorescence analysis demonstrated increased positive cell index (PCI) values for p53, PUMA, and Bax alongside decreased Bcl-2 PCI in the AKI group (p < 0.05), while NOXA PCI remained unchanged (p > 0.05). Notably, melatonin administration resulted in a statistically significant reduction in the Bax/Bcl-2 ratio compared to the untreated AKI group (p < 0.05), indicating a shift toward cellular survival at the protein level. No statistically significant differences were detected in apoptotic gene expression at the mRNA level. Serum creatinine levels increased significantly in the AKI group (p < 0.001). Melatonin treatment is associated with a modulation of key components within the p53-PUMA/Bcl-2-Bax apoptotic signaling axis in renal tissue following ischemia-reperfusion injury.

articles.title: Design and characterization of lopinavir-loaded microspheres: linking drug-polymer interactions with sustained release and HIV-1 protease inhibition.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to develop a sustained-release drug delivery system for lopinavir (LPV) using cellulose acetate (CA)-based microspheres to enhance drug dissolution and physical stability. LPV-loaded microspheres were prepared via an oil-in-water (O/W) emulsion solvent evaporation method and characterized using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and near-infrared (NIR) chemical imaging. Solid-state characterization confirmed successful encapsulation and revealed that the crystalline drug was converted into a high-energy amorphous molecular dispersion within the CA polymeric matrix, showing excellent drug-polymer chemical compatibility. In vitro dissolution profiles demonstrated sustained drug release over 24 h, with formulations LPV-MCs (R4, R9, and R10, all prepared at a 1:1 drug-to-polymer ratio and a stirring speed of 1000 rpm, varying in surfactant concentration [0.1 to 0.5%] and stirring time [4 to 6 h]) showing the highest dissolution rates, achieving 75.82%, 62.40%, and 62.70% drug release after 24 h, respectively. Morphological analysis via SEM revealed regular spherical microspheres with progressive surface porosity that directly modulated the sustained drug release behavior through matrix diffusion. In silico molecular docking simulations predicted strong binding affinities and hydrogen-bonding networks between the active lopinavir molecules and the catalytic pocket of the target HIV-1 protease enzyme (yielding a free binding energy of - 7.064 kcal/mol). Furthermore, 3D pharmacophore modeling and matrix-docking evaluations supported a highly compatible host-guest relationship between the drug and the cellulose acetate subunits, explaining the high physical entrapment efficiency. These findings highlight the critical role of drug-polymer structural compatibility in modulating sustained drug release and maintaining the chemical integrity of the active pharmaceutical ingredient, validating LPV-loaded CA microspheres as a promising multiparticulate platform for optimized oral HIV therapy.

articles.title: Physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling to predict sumatriptan pharmacokinetics across OCT1 functional groups.
articles.abstract: Sumatriptan is a 5-hydroxytryptamine 1B/1D receptor agonist for acute migraine. Reduced organic cation transporter 1 (OCT1) function is associated with increased sumatriptan exposure, but its quantitative contribution to pharmacokinetic variability remains unclear. The aim of the study is to develop a whole-body physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model describing sumatriptan PK across OCT1 functional groups and explore an exposure-matched candidate dose. A 50-mg mixed-genotype base model was developed from three clinical studies and extrapolated to 25 and 100 mg without reestimating drug-specific parameters. OCT1 functional differences were represented by changes in the effective OCT1-mediated hepatic uptake capacity (Vmax). Individuals with 0 active OCT1 alleles were compared with those with 1 or 2 active alleles. Oral doses of 20, 25, and 30 mg were explored in the 0-active-allele group using a predefined exposure-matching range of 0.80-1.25 for Cmax and AUC0-9 h. Across 50-mg studies, geometric mean fold errors were 1.25 for Cmax, 1.07 for AUC0-12 h, and 1.12 for Tmax. Across 25- and 100-mg studies, predicted-to-observed ratios ranged from 0.65 to 1.50. After 50 mg, predicted Cmax and AUC0-9 h ratios for the 0-active-allele group relative to the 1-or-2-active-allele group were 1.81 and 1.82, compared with observed ratios of 1.77 and 2.20. Both 25 and 30 mg in the 0-active-allele group met the predefined exposure-matching criterion relative to 50 mg in the 1-or-2-active-allele group, whereas 20 mg did not.The PBPK model quantified OCT1-related variability in sumatriptan disposition and supported 25 mg as a clinically feasible exploratory candidate for prospective evaluation in the 0-active-allele group.

articles.title: A synbiotic nanoemulsion modulates metabolic dysfunction and organ functioning in high-fat diet-induced obese mice.
articles.abstract: High-fat diet (HFD)-induced obesity is associated with metabolic disturbance and structural changes in the intestine, liver, kidney, and adipose tissue. This study evaluated the effects of a co-formulated nanoemulsion containing silk fibroin (a proposed prebiotic) and Lactobacillus rhamnosus (a probiotic), referred to here as a synbiotic nanoemulsion, in HFD-induced obese mice. A synbiotic nanoemulsion was prepared using a high-energy method and characterized by UV-visible spectroscopy and FTIR analysis. Forty-eight male mice were randomly divided into eight groups (n = 6) and fed different diet for 16 weeks. Body weight was recorded weekly, following biochemical, histological, and histomorphometric analysis. Compared with the normal diet group (31.82 ± 1.18 g), HFD-fed mice showed a significant increase in body weight (48.7 ± 0.07 g) and severe dyslipidemia, evidenced by elevated total cholesterol (222-276.5 mg/dL), triglycerides (195-289.5 mg/dL), and low-density lipoprotein (104.8-140 mg/dL), with reduced high-density lipoprotein levels (9-23 mg/dL). Synbiotic supplementation significantly reduced blood urea nitrogen (8-10 mg/dL), serum creatinine (0.55-1.0 mg/dL), alanine aminotransferase (28-39 U/L), and aspartate aminotransferase (129-141 U/L). Furthermore, systemic inflammation was also reduced reflected by lowered TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β, alongside increased IL-10 levels as compared to HFD group. Histological and histomorphometric analysis showed improved organ architecture in the synbiotic-treated group, with several measurements close to those of the normal diet group. In this HFD mouse model, the fibroin-L. rhamnosus nanoemulsion was associated with lower body weight, improved lipid profile, liver, kidney, and inflammatory markers, and improved tissue morphology. These findings support further study of the formulation. The design does not allow conclusions about synergy, nanoemulsion-specific delivery effects or mechanisms.

articles.title: Microbiome-Mediated Pharmacokinetics and Informed Dosing of Mycophenolate in Kidney Transplantation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The gut microbiome contributes to interindividual variability in drug pharmacokinetics; however, its role in guiding dose adjustments remains unclear. Mycophenolic acid (MPA), the active metabolite of the immunosuppressant mycophenolate mofetil (MMF), exhibits high pharmacokinetic variability, potentially linked to microbial activity. This study aimed to characterize the gut microbiome effect on MPA pharmacokinetics and determine if these effects necessitate dose modifications. METHODS: In 84 kidney transplant recipients, plasma and urine concentration-time profiles for MPA and its glucuronide metabolites were characterized using population pharmacokinetic modeling in NONMEM®. Stool samples were collected within 2 days of pharmacokinetic sampling for microbiome shotgun metagenomic sequencing. Machine learning was used to identify microbial species associated with pharmacokinetic variability. The impact of these species and clinical covariates was evaluated using full fixed-effect modeling. Simulations were conducted to assess the effect of microbial relative abundance on MPA therapeutic target attainment across various MMF doses. RESULTS: Five bacteria were associated with the magnitude or duration of enterohepatic circulation (EHC). High relative abundance of Eubacterium callanderi increased EHC and MPA exposure by 29-63%, requiring a 17% lower MMF dose. Conversely, high Faecalibacterium SGB15315 abundance reduced EHC and MPA exposure by 13-26%, requiring a 50-75% higher dose. While Gemmiger formicilis and Eisenbergiella tayi prolonged EHC by >100% and Anaerostipes caccae decreased it by 30%, these taxa did not clinically impact therapeutic target attainment. CONCLUSION: We identified several stool microbial species affecting MPA pharmacokinetics. Specifically, Eubacterium callanderi and Faecalibacterium SGB15315 may identify patients who require additional therapeutic drug monitoring or possible dose modifications to reach target concentrations. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov, NCT04953715.

articles.title: Safety and tolerability study of subcutaneous injections of larger volumes in abdominal and lower extremity sites suitable for autoinjectors.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study investigated pain and safety of subcutaneous injections, using larger volumes (>3 mL) and injection rates. METHODS: 32 subjects were recruited and had 4 injections: 2.5, 5.0, 10.0, and 15 mL administered in the abdomen and thigh using an infusion pump. Injection force was measured and pain assessments obtained using VAS (0-100 mm), and verbal pain ratings. RESULTS: All 125 infusions appropriately delivered the complete volume. VAS pain increased after start of injections: median VAS: 10.00 mm (IQR: 1.50-27.00) and peaked to 16 mm (IQR: 8.50-43.50) at 4 min for the 15 mL infusions. Median VAS after termination of infusions was 6.5 mm (IQR: 0-18). Verbal pain at start of injection was none to mild. VAS pain ratings were higher (p < 0.001) for 0.500 mL/sec and 0.333 mL/sec infusion rates compared to 0.023 mL/sec. Peak injection forces were significantly (p < 0.001) different from one another for the three infusion rates with a moderate correlation (R = 0.55, p < 0.001) between injection force and pain. Minimal saline leaked onto the skin surface for all volumes and delivery rates. CONCLUSION: These results provide evidence that subcutaneous administration of >3 mL volumes into the subcutaneous tissue of the abdomen or thigh, was safe and well tolerated. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT06194578.

articles.title: 1-Methylhistidine attenuates early myocardial inflammation in type 3 cardiorenal syndrome through modulation of the p105/p50 NF-κB axis.
