articles.abstract: Type 3 cardiorenal syndrome (CRS3) is characterized by cardiac injury or dysfunction secondary to acute kidney injury (AKI), yet the contribution of AKI-associated metabolic remodeling to early myocardial inflammation remains poorly understood. Here, paired serum and myocardial untargeted metabolomics identified 1-methylhistidine (1-MH) as a metabolite elevated in both compartments, with the highest variable importance in projection score in serum. Exogenous 1-MH improved the E/A ratio and attenuated myocardial inflammation and terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick-end labeling (TUNEL) positivity in rats with CRS3. Similar protective effects were observed in a separate post-ischemic cohort in which 1-MH was administered immediately after renal reperfusion. In CRS serum-exposed H9c2 cells, 1-MH reduced reactive oxygen species-associated fluorescence, malondialdehyde content, and intracellular Fe2+ levels. Transcriptomic profiling showed that 1-MH suppressed inflammatory signaling, accompanied by changes in oxidative metabolism. Integration of these transcriptomic signatures with target prediction prioritized NFKB1/p105, while ensemble docking identified recurrent candidate interaction regions within p105. Cellular thermal shift assays showed a concentration-related increase in p105 thermal stability following 1-MH treatment. 1-MH increased p105 abundance while reducing total p50 abundance and nuclear p50 accumulation. p105 overexpression increased p50 abundance and the expression of inflammatory transcripts and proteins suppressed by 1-MH. These findings demonstrate that 1-MH attenuates early myocardial inflammation in CRS3 and reduces oxidative stress-related changes in CRS serum-exposed H9c2 cells. These functional results support modulation of the p105/p50 NF-κB axis and identify p105 as a molecular link between AKI-associated metabolic remodeling and myocardial inflammatory signaling.

articles.title: Optimization of direct oral anticoagulant prescribing in primary care: a pharmacotherapeutic review in real-world clinical practice and therapeutic efficiency.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Direct oral anticoagulants are among the first-line treatments for stroke prevention in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation and for the treatment and secondary prevention of venous thromboembolism. The increasing use of these agents poses challenges related to prescribing appropriateness, clinical safety. This study aims to evaluate the impact of a primary care pharmacist-led intervention on the appropriateness of DOAC prescribing, pharmacotherapeutic efficiency, and clinical outcomes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective, quasi-experimental before-and-after study was conducted in the healthcare area of Xarxa Santa Tecla (Tarragonès and Baix Penedès, Spain). 791 patients receiving DOAC therapy were included. The intervention comprised multidisciplinary educational activities, individualized pharmacotherapeutic review, and communication of recommendations to prescribers. RESULTS: The mean age was 78.2 years, and 43.2% of patients had moderate or severe renal impairment. The pharmacotherapeutic review identified 527 patients (66.6%) as candidates for treatment optimization, through a proposed switch from apixaban to dabigatran. The pharmacist intervention was associated with changes in prescribing patterns among newly initiated patients, increasing the use of dabigatran. The economic analysis estimated savings of €75,508.81 from new treatment initiations and €31,288.25 from therapeutic switches, resulting in total savings of €106,797.06 in 2025. The overall bleeding rate remained stable (5.3% in 2024% vs. 5.2% in 2025), with no deterioration in clinical safety. In conclusion, a structured, multidisciplinary, and coordinated primary care pharmacist-led intervention promoted a more efficient use of healthcare resources, while no deterioration in population-level safety indicators was observed. These findings reinforce the role of primary care pharmacists in optimizing anticoagulant therapy.

articles.title: Cucurbitacin B suppresses GBM progression by inducing GADD45α-Dependent PCNA downregulation and DNA replication arrest.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most aggressive primary brain tumor, characterized by uncontrolled proliferation and resistance to current standard chemoradiotherapy. Natural products have emerged as promising anticancer agents, yet the therapeutic mechanisms of Cucurbitacin B (CuB), a highly bioactive triterpenoid, in GBM remain insufficiently understood. Our preliminary transcriptomic analysis revealed that CuB markedly upregulates GADD45α while suppressing PCNA, suggesting a previously unrecognized replication-stress regulatory axis. PURPOSE: This study aimed to determine the anti-GBM efficacy of CuB across bulk and stem-like tumor models and to elucidate the molecular cascade connecting GADD45α induction to PCNA-mediated DNA replication arrest. METHODS: The anti-tumor effects of CuB were evaluated in GBM cell lines (LN229, U87) and patient-derived glioma stem cells (GSCs) via functional assays, flow cytometry, and extreme limiting dilution assays. Transcriptome sequencing guided mechanistic exploration. Gain- and loss-of-function assays (GADD45α knockdown/overexpression, PCNA overexpression) elucidated the signaling cascade. Therapeutic efficacy was assessed in an orthotopic GBM xenograft mouse model. RESULTS: CuB significantly suppressed the malignant phenotypes of GBM cells and impaired the self-renewal capacity of GSCs, concomitantly inducing apoptosis and G2/M-phase arrest, as evidenced by Cyclin B1 suppression and CDK1 inhibitory phosphorylation. Mechanistically, CuB strongly upregulated GADD45α, which maintained the Retinoblastoma (Rb) protein in a hypophosphorylated, active state. Active Rb subsequently sequestered the E2F1 transcription factor, leading to the profound transcriptional downregulation of PCNA. Knockdown of GADD45α restored Rb/E2F1-driven PCNA expression and reversed CuB-mediated replication arrest, whereas GADD45α overexpression phenocopied CuB. Ectopic PCNA expression counteracted these suppressive effects. In vivo, CuB effectively reduced intracranial tumor burden and prolonged survival in a GADD45α-dependent manner, while exhibiting a highly favorable systemic safety profile in healthy mice. CONCLUSION: CuB suppresses GBM progression by activating GADD45α, which targets the Rb/E2F1 signaling axis to transcriptionally repress PCNA-mediated DNA replication. These findings highlight the GADD45α-Rb/E2F1-PCNA cascade as a critical mechanistic vulnerability and position CuB as a safe, promising replication-modulating agent for highly heterogeneous GBM.

articles.title: Retraction: A comparative randomized clinical trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of tacrolimus versus hydrocortisone as a topical treatment of atopic dermatitis in children.
