articles.title: Ferumoxytol potentiates ferroptotic radiosensitization through NCOA4-associated iron mobilization in brain-metastatic lung cancer cells.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Brain metastasis remains a major cause of mortality in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer, whereas effective radiosensitization strategies are constrained by heterogeneous tumor responses and the tolerance of normal brain tissue. Ferumoxytol, a clinically used iron oxide nanoparticle formulation, has emerging translational potential as an iron-modulating agent. However, whether Ferumoxytol enhances radiosensitivity in brain-metastatic lung cancer cells and the mechanisms underlying this effect remain unclear. METHODS: PC-9 lung adenocarcinoma cells and NCI-H1915 brain-metastatic lung adenocarcinoma cells were used to evaluate ferumoxytol under basal and irradiated conditions. Ferroptosis-associated phenotypes, oxidative stress, clonogenic survival, and cell-cycle distribution were assessed. TMT-based proteomics and public single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses were used for candidate prioritization and disease-context support. NCOA4 was evaluated by siRNA-mediated loss of function, single-dose clonogenic assays, time-resolved NCOA4/FTH1 immunoblotting, bafilomycin A1-based autophagic-flux analysis, and endogenous NCOA4-FTH1 co-immunoprecipitation. RESULTS: Ferumoxytol induced mitochondrial, biochemical, and molecular changes consistent with ferroptosis and enhanced irradiation-associated ROS accumulation, lipid peroxidation, and loss of clonogenic survival. Proteomic analysis prioritized NCOA4, while public transcriptomic analyses provided associative disease-context support. In H1915 cells, NCOA4 silencing attenuated combined-treatment Fe2+ accumulation, oxidative stress, and γ-H2AX induction. The incremental reduction in colony formation produced by adding ferumoxytol to irradiation was also reduced after NCOA4 knockdown in H1915 cells and was no longer significant in PC-9 cells. Time-resolved immunoblotting showed marked FTH1 accumulation rather than net FTH1 depletion, with a late reduction in NCOA4. Bafilomycin A1 caused further LC3B-II and SQSTM1/p62 accumulation under IR + F, consistent with ongoing autophagic turnover, whereas co-immunoprecipitation showed greater normalized recovery of FTH1 in NCOA4 immunoprecipitates after IR + F. CONCLUSION: Ferumoxytol enhances ferroptosis-associated oxidative injury and radiosensitivity in the tested lung cancer cell models. The combined loss-of-function, autophagic-flux, and protein-interaction data support the involvement of NCOA4-associated ferritin handling and iron mobilization. However, the observed FTH1 accumulation and the absence of iron-chelator rescue, cargo-specific lysosomal tracking, and in vivo validation preclude a definitive claim of canonical ferritinophagy or clinical efficacy.

articles.title: Circ_0024390 promotes renal tubular EMT through the miR-6890-3p/CHD4 axis: implications for renal interstitial fibrosis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Renal interstitial fibrosis (RIF) is a central pathological event in the progression of various chronic kidney diseases (CKD) to end-stage renal disease, for which effective therapeutic strategies remain lacking. Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) of renal tubular epithelial cells serves as a pivotal mechanism driving RIF. While circular RNAs (circRNAs) have been implicated in various pathological processes, their specific roles and underlying mechanisms in the progression of RIF remain incompletely elucidated. METHODS: A circRNA microarray was utilized to screen differentially expressed circRNAs in a TGF-β1-induced HK-2 cell model of renal fibrosis. Loss-of-function experiments were performed to explore the biological effects of circ_0024390 on renal tubular EMT, as well as the proliferation and migration of HK-2 cells. Mechanistic assays were further conducted to verify the competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) regulatory mechanism of circ_0024390. RESULTS: Circ_0024390 was significantly upregulated in the in vitro fibrosis model, specifically in TGF-β1-induced HK-2 cells. Functional studies demonstrated that knockdown of circ_0024390 effectively attenuated renal tubular EMT and inhibited key cellular processes, including proliferation and migration. Mechanistic investigations further revealed that circ_0024390 functioned as a ceRNA by sponging miR-6890-3p. This sponging relieved the repressive effect of miR-6890-3p on its downstream target, chromodomain helicase DNA-binding protein 4 (CHD4), leading to the upregulation of CHD4 expression. CONCLUSION: These findings delineate a novel circ_0024390/miR-6890-3p/CHD4 axis that promotes EMT in renal tubular epithelial cells and contributes to the progression of RIF. This study provides new insights into the pathogenesis of RIF and highlights circ_0024390 as a potential promising therapeutic target for CKD.

articles.title: Emodin attenuates CFA-induced inflammatory pain in association with suppression of the Cx3cl1/Cx3cr1/p38 MAPK signaling axis.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the analgesic effect of emodin on Complete Freund's Adjuvant (CFA)-induced inflammatory pain and to clarify the underlying molecular mechanism. METHODS: Emodin was administered intraperitoneally or prophylactically to attenuate CFA-induced inflammatory pain. RNA-seq was performed to identify the biological functions of differentially expressed genes in mouse dorsal root ganglion (DRG) tissues. The expression levels of Cx3cl1/Cx3cr1 were evaluated by RT-qPCR, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence. Pharmacological and genetic approaches were employed to block Cx3cr1 and assess its effect on pain thresholds in CFA-treated mice. Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining was used to examine the infiltration of immune and inflammatory cells in dorsal root ganglion (DRG) tissues before and after emodin treatment. Following emodin treatment, the levels of p-p38/p38 in DRG tissues were determined by Western blotting, and the mRNA levels of the pro-inflammatory cytokines Tnf-α, Il-1β, and Il-6 in DRG tissues were measured by RT-qPCR. RESULTS: Both therapeutic and prophylactic administration of emodin effectively alleviated CFA-induced mechanical and thermal hypersensitivity. Emodin treatment suppressed the CFA-induced upregulation of Cx3cl1/Cx3cr1 mRNA and protein levels in the DRG. Pharmacological and genetic blockade of Cx3cr1 effectively attenuated CFA-induced hyperalgesia. In addition, emodin markedly inhibited p-p38/p38 protein expression in the DRG of mice with CFA-induced inflammatory pain, reduced immune cell infiltration in DRG tissues, and downregulated the levels of the pro-inflammatory cytokines Tnf-α, Il-1β, and Il-6. CONCLUSION: Emodin attenuated CFA-induced inflammatory pain in mice, an effect associated with reduced Cx3cl1/Cx3cr1 signaling, decreased p38 MAPK activation, diminished immune-cell infiltration in the DRG, and lower expression of the proinflammatory cytokines Tnf-α, Il-1β, and Il-6 in DRG tissue.

articles.title: CT habitat and peritumoral radiomics for predicting progression after repeat TACE in hepatocellular carcinoma: a multicenter study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: This study developed and validated an machine-learning-based radiomics model integrating tumor habitat radiomics, peritumoral radiomics, and clinical features to predict progression-free survival (PFS) following repeat transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study included 270 patients with HCC. Patients from Center 1 were assigned to training (n = 94) and internal validation (n = 41) cohorts, while Centers 2 (n = 82) and 3 (n = 53) served as external validation cohorts. Tumor habitats and 5-mm peritumoral regions were generated from contrast-enhanced CT images. Radiomics features were selected using univariate Cox and LASSO-Cox regression. A fusion model and HPC risk score were constructed by integrating selected radiomics signatures and clinical variables. Performance was assessed using time-dependent ROC, C-index, calibration, decision curve analysis, and Kaplan-Meier analyses. RESULTS: The optimal habitat cluster number was K = 2. Eleven habitat features, three peritumoral features, and alpha-fetoprotein were retained in the fusion model. The model achieved AUCs of 0.923, 0.921, and 0.897 for 3-, 6-, and 9-month progression-free survival in the training cohort, and 0.932, 0.863, and 0.916 in the internal validation cohort, respectively; all external AUCs exceeded 0.82. The fusion model showed higher C-index values than the clinical model across cohorts. High-risk patients had significantly shorter PFS than low-risk patients (all P < 0.001). Calibration and decision curve analyses demonstrated good agreement and clinical utility. CONCLUSION: The CT-based fusion model and HPC risk score effectively predicted progression risk in HCC.

articles.title: Extrachromosomal circular DNA drives focal amplification of AGAP2-AS1 to promote cutaneous tumorigenesis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Extrachromosomal circular DNA (eccDNA) represents a pervasive structural continuum of genomic instability that drives intratumoral heterogeneity; the topography of the eccDNA-encoded non-coding transcriptome remains obscure in ultraviolet (UV)-driven malignancies. METHODS: We profiled eccDNA from Basal Cell Carcinoma, Inverted Follicular Keratosis, Merkel Cell Carcinoma, and matched adjacent normal tissues using Circle-Seq. Structural data were integrated with the eccDNA Gene Analyzer (ECGA) and The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) clinical cohorts. In vitro siRNA-mediated knockdown assays were used to determine the oncogenic functionality of identified lncRNAs. RESULTS: Circle-Seq revealed genome-wide remodeling of circular DNA with focal hyper-amplification, GC-rich compositional biases, and recurrent hotspots on chromosomes 9, 16, and 20. Integrative screening identified AGAP2-AS1 as a clinically significant, copy-number-associated lncRNA, whose expression correlated with cellular responses to UV radiation and oxidative stress. Depletion of AGAP2-AS1 impaired tumor cell proliferation, migration, and invasion in vitro. CONCLUSION: The eccDNA landscape serves as a reservoir of functional non-coding elements; focal amplification of AGAP2-AS1 contributes to malignant progression and stress adaptation in cutaneous neoplasia.

articles.title: A diarylheptanoid from Alpinia officinarum ameliorates insulin resistance in 3T3-L1 adipocytes and db/db mice through modulation of PPARγ/PI3K/AKT signaling pathway.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Alpinia officinarum Hance and its diarylheptanoid metabolite, (R)-5-hydroxy-1,7-diphenyl-3-heptanone (DPHC), have hypoglycemic and hypolipidemic effects to ameliorate T2DM with insulin resistance (IR). However, the mechanisms by which DPHC ameliorates adipose IR associated with lipid metabolism disorders are not yet fully elucidated. METHODS: DPHC was evaluated in dexamethasone-induced IR-3T3-L1 adipocytes and db/db mice. Exploratory network analysis was used to generate candidate mechanisms. RESULTS: In IR-3T3-L1 adipocytes, DPHC increased glucose consumption and 2-NBDG uptake, reduced lipid accumulation and inflammatory-marker expression, and increased measured PPARγ and insulin-signaling-associated molecular markers. GW9662 attenuated several cellular effects of DPHC, supporting the involvement of a PPARγ-dependent component. In db/db mice, oral DPHC administration at 80 or 140 mg/kg/day reduced lipid accumulation and improved measured serum lipid-related endpoints. Pocket-directed docking to the DPHC-bound PPARγ ligand-binding domain, together with a single 100-ns molecular-dynamics trajectory, generated a structurally plausible binding pose. CONCLUSION: The findings support a testable model in which DPHC may alleviate adipocyte insulin resistance partly through PPARγ-associated PI3K/AKT regulation.

articles.title: The reporting phenotype of penile fracture after collagenase clostridium histolyticum for Peyronie's disease: an indication-restricted FAERS study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Corporal rupture and severe penile injury are established complications of collagenase clostridium histolyticum (CCH) treatment for Peyronie's disease. How spontaneous reports jointly encode injury, management, hospitalization, timing, and procedural or product-use details remains unclear. METHODS: We analyzed quarterly FDA Adverse Event Reporting System files from 2014Q1 through 2025Q4. We retained the latest, deletion-list-aware report version when CCH was the primary suspect for a strict Peyronie's disease indication. We compared a fracture-coded phenotype (F1) with a mutually exclusive non-fracture local-injury phenotype (I1). Raw report proportions with exact confidence intervals were the primary descriptive results. Firth models provided secondary control for reporting period, healthcare professional reporter, and manufacturer origin. Analyses also considered surgery/repair (M1), hospitalization, a heterogeneous procedural/product-use summary (P1), and a report-level therapy-start-to-event interval. RESULTS: Of 3,750 latest-version strict reports, 3,658 named CCH as the sole primary suspect. The active comparison included 445 F1 and 834 I1 reports. M1 was recorded in 194/445 F1 and 30/834 I1 reports. Hospitalization was recorded in 2.5% of I1 reports without M1, 8.0% of F1 reports without M1, and 26.3% of F1 reports with M1. P1 was recorded in 57/445 F1 reports (12.8%, exact 95% CI: 9.8%-16.3%) and 171/834 I1 reports (20.5%, 17.8%-23.4%); the crude odds ratio was 0.57 (exact 95% CI: 0.40-0.80), and the adjusted reporting odds ratio was 0.50 (95% CI: 0.35-0.71). The subdomains were directionally discordant. After 20 P1-negative F1 reports were reclassified, the balanced adjusted 95% CI included 1; reclassification of 35 reports equalized the crude proportions. A therapy-start-to-event interval was available for 91/445 F1 reports (median 14 days, IQR 1-27), and entry into this date-complete subset was non-random. CONCLUSION: Fracture-coded FAERS reports after CCH form a clinically coherent but heterogeneous phenotype, often accompanied by surgery/repair or hospitalization codes. P1 is a reporting-process summary rather than a unitary clinical construct: its inverse aggregate association concealed discordant components, was sensitive to modest differential under-recording, and does not indicate protection. The study refines the reporting phenotype of a known serious risk without estimating incidence, comparative safety, or causation.

articles.title: AB-free Kava reduces anxiety-like behavior without preventing nicotine-induced exploration suppression in mice.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Tobacco use is the leading preventable cause of death worldwide. Anxiety increases the risk for smoking, and smoking in turn increases the risk for anxiety disorders. There is therefore a need to identify interventions that reduce anxiety, in general and in the context of smoking. Kava (Piper methysticum), a natural product with a long history of indigenous use, has been shown to have anxiolytic and calming effects and reduce nicotine withdrawal. The current study examined whether kava without the hepatotoxic flavokavains A and B (AB-free) could reduce anxiety-like behavior in mice repeatedly treated with nicotine. METHODS: Male and female C57BL/6N mice received either a control diet or an AB-free kava-supplemented diet and underwent two blocks of nicotine treatments. Mice underwent a first block of five every-other-day injections of nicotine (0.5 mg/kg) or saline, with open field testing after each injection, followed 1 week later by a nicotine challenge. A second block of injections was given using the same injection schedule, followed by a second challenge 1 week later, and 2 weeks afterward mice received a final challenge in a novel open field. RESULTS: During the first treatment block, nicotine significantly reduced locomotor activity and center time. There was a significant diet × treatment interaction on center time, with AB-free kava significantly increasing center time in saline-treated but not nicotine-treated mice. During the final challenge in a novel open field, nicotine again significantly reduced locomotor activity and center time, and AB-free kava significantly increased center time irrespective of nicotine treatment, without affecting locomotor activity. These effects remained significant when cage was included as a random factor. DISCUSSION: These results suggest that AB-free kava has anxiolytic-like effects without reducing locomotor activity but does not prevent nicotine-induced suppression of exploratory behavior.

articles.title: Harnessing marine polysaccharides for breast cancer therapy: ulvan synergizes with nano-selenium to induce programmed cell death through dual modulation of autophagy and apoptosis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Since breast cancer is one of the biggest worldwide health issues, new and effective treatment approaches are required. Because autophagy control has two context-dependent roles in the development of cancer, it is a prospective therapeutic target. With an emphasis on the regulation of oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis, and autophagy, this work assessed the anticancer potential of ulvan, a sulfated polysaccharide produced from Ulva lactuca, and ulvan-loaded nano-selenium in an Ehrlich solid carcinoma model. MATERIAL: ESC-bearing mice were treated with ulvan extract, sodium selenite or ulvan-SeNPs for 14 days. The anticancer activity was assessed through histology, oxidative stress markers, inflammatory mediators, apoptotic proteins and genes expression for autophagy and molecular docking studies. RESULTS: Molecular docking analysis revealed ulvan-derived saccharides to bind strongly to VEGFR2, CD44 and Toll-like receptors suggesting multi-target action. Ulvan in vivo restored antioxidant defenses, reduced oxidative stress and inflammatory markers and induced apoptosis via caspase-3, Bcl-2 and Bax modulation. Ulvan induced controlled autophagy by decreasing mTOR and increasing autophagy related gene expression. Ulvan-SeNPs exhibited enhanced anticancer activity with increased activation of autophagic and apoptotic pathways, as evidenced by tumor shrinkage, reduced angiogenesis and histopathological analysis. CONCLUSION: Ulvan is a controlled anti-cancer agent, with a mechanism synergistically enhanced by nano-selenium. These results indicate that ulvan could be a potential natural therapeutic for breast cancer alone or in combination with nano-selenium.

articles.title: Characterization and technical evaluation of physicochemical properties of Tibetan medicine Zuotai via modern processing.
articles.abstract: Zuotai, known as the "king of medicines" in Tibetan pharmacology, is a crucial ingredient in precious formulations such as Seventy-flavor Pearl Pills. Traditional preparation of Zuotai is complex, time-consuming, labor-intensive, and poses significant toxicity risks. To address these challenges, our research team has modernized the process by replacing traditional tools with jacketed reactors and controlled heating, significantly reducing toxicity, shortening processing time from over 40 days to about 20 days, and enhancing reproducibility. In this study, five batches of Zuotai samples were characterized using X-ray fluorescence (XRF), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR). Results confirmed consistent physicochemical properties across all batches, dominated by HgS with excess sulfur. Safety evaluation via in vitro simulated gastric/intestinal fluid dissolution tests demonstrated that the soluble mercury release from modern-processed Zuotai was only 38.64 μg/g (0.0258% of total Hg) under the most stringent conditions (SGF with 10 mM L-cysteine, 37 °C, 24 h), corresponding to a daily intake of approximately 7.73 μg-only 18% of the FAO/WHO acceptable daily intake (43 μg/day), offering a standardized approach for Zuotai production.

articles.title: Entresto attenuates dexamethasone-induced metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic features in rats: role of potential SGK1/FOXO3a regulatory pathway and cardio-metabolic axis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Prolonged or high dexamethasone (DEXA) exposure can promote steatohepatitis-like liver injury through insulin resistance, oxidative stress, inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and fibrosis. Sacubitril/valsartan (Entresto) exhibits metabolic, anti-inflammatory, and antifibrotic properties that may protect against glucocorticoid-induced hepatic injury. The current study investigates the protective effects of Entresto against DEXA-induced hepatic injury in rats. METHODS: Male rats were assigned into control, DEXA, and DEXA-treated groups receiving Entresto (30 or 60 mg/kg). Liver function, metabolic parameters, oxidative stress biomarkers, inflammatory and angiogenic mediators, fibrosis-related markers, and key signaling pathways were assessed using biochemical, molecular, histopathological, and immunohistochemical analyses. RESULTS: DEXA administration induced hepatic injury, as evidenced by significant elevation of serum ALT, AST, and LDH levels and significant reduction in albumin concentration, accompanied by marked histopathological abnormalities. DEXA also promoted insulin resistance as reflected by increased fasting glucose, insulin, HOMA-IR and impaired OGTT. These changes were accompanied by metabolic dysregulation, including increased PEPCK and GSK expression, reduced glycogen synthase expression, elevated free fatty acids and oxidized LDL, and reduced PPAR-γ and PGC1-α. DEXA further altered IRS-1/AKT/JNK/p-AMPK/FOXO3 signaling, increased oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction, enhanced inflammatory cytokine production and macrophage activation, and upregulated fibrosis-related mediators and renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) activation. In addition, DEXA increased SGK1, TRAF1, and SETD7 expression. Entresto treatment significantly attenuated DEXA-induced hepatic injury improved metabolic homeostasis and insulin sensitivity, enhanced antioxidant defenses, reduced inflammatory and fibrotic responses, and suppressed RAAS overactivation. These effects were associated with modulation of SGK1/FOXO3a signaling and activation of AMPK and PPAR γ-related pathways. CONCLUSION: ENT attenuates DEXA-induced metabolic liver injury with steatotic features by restoring insulin sensitivity, normalizing hepatic triglyceride accumulation, reducing oxidative stress, and modulating inflammatory and pro-fibrotic tissue markers, potentially through regulation of the SGK1/FOXO3a and cGMP/PKG/AMPK pathways crosstalk. These findings suggest that Entresto represents a promising therapeutic approach for mitigating glucocorticoid-induced steatohepatitis-like metabolic liver injury.

articles.title: Associations between redox-related biomarkers and treatment response in patients with inflammatory bowel disease initiating infliximab or vedolizumab.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Oxidative stress is increasingly recognized as a key component of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) pathophysiology, yet the clinical relevance of systemic redox biomarkers during biologic therapy remains poorly understood. In this exploratory study, we investigated whether systemic redox biomarkers are associated with short-term and long-term response to infliximab (IFX) or vedolizumab (VEDO) and their relationship with iron metabolism. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patients with active IBD initiating induction therapy with IFX or VEDO were included. Serum redox biomarkers (cysteine, homocysteine, free thiols (FTs), glutathione, and thioredoxin-1), inflammatory markers, and iron parameters were measured at baseline and during induction therapy. Patients were stratified according to short-term clinical response at week 14 and long-term response at 1 year. Longitudinal mixed-effects models, correlation analyses, and logistic regression were used to evaluate associations between redox biomarkers, treatment outcomes, and iron metabolism. RESULTS: Fifty-eight patients were included (IFX: n = 37; VEDO: n = 21). Induction therapy resulted in marked reductions in inflammatory markers in short-term responders. Redox biomarkers showed more modest, mostly non-significant, response-dependent patterns. IFX-treated short-term non-responders exhibited non-significant lower cysteine levels than responders at baseline (2,336 vs. 3,611 μg/mL; p > 0.05) and week 14 (2,888 vs. 3,599 μg/mL; p > 0.05). Similarly, homocysteine levels were higher in IFX-treated short-term non-responders at baseline (7,500 vs. 4,260 ng/mL; p < 0.05) and week 14 (7,002 vs. 4,278 ng/mL; p > 0.05), whereas VEDO-treated patients showed comparable levels between response groups. FT levels showed no significant changes, increasing in short-term responders while decreasing in short-term non-responders across both therapies. Glutathione levels showed no major overall changes, although levels between IFX-treated long-term responders and non-responders appeared to differ during induction therapy. Glutathione correlated inversely with transferrin saturation (r = -0.50, p < 0.05) and serum iron (r = -0.46, p < 0.05) after induction therapy. CONCLUSION: Exploratory analyses suggested treatment response-related differences in cysteine, homocysteine, and FTs in IFX-treated patients, highlighting their potential as biomarkers of treatment response that warrant further investigation. Glutathione demonstrated an association with iron metabolism, suggesting a different biological role. These findings suggest a potential role for redox-iron interactions in treatment response biology that warrant further exploration and validation in larger prospective cohorts.

articles.title: Cuban epidemic neuropathy: lessons learned from scientific and political controversies.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Cuban epidemic neuropathy (CEN), which emerged in the early 1990s during Cuba's Special Period, was one of the largest neurological epidemics of the 20th century and became the subject of a scientific and political controversy. OBJECTIVE: To revisit the epidemic and examine the lessons learned from the scientific debates, institutional responses, and political context that shaped its investigation and management. DEVELOPMENT: This perspective integrates epidemiological, clinical, neuropathological, therapeutic and health evidence, to analyze competing etiological hypotheses and the influence of geopolitical and institutional factors on scientific interpretation. Accumulated evidence-including severe dietary restriction, depletion of B-group vitamins and other nutrients, increased metabolic demands, tobacco and alcohol exposure, and axonal pathology-supports a multifactorial toxic-nutritional model, over a viral agent. Nutritional depletion may have reduced mitochondrial metabolic reserve, antioxidant and detoxification capacity, and increased oxidative stress. Mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative injury provide a convergent mechanism for selective vulnerability of the optic nerve and peripheral axons. Therapeutic implications underscore the benefit of early nutritional intervention even when the specific contributions of individual nutrients or toxins remain uncertain. The scientific controversy illustrates how geopolitical and institutional factors influenced the interpretation of science, research priorities, communication, and public health decision-making. CONCLUSION: CEN demonstrates the importance of multidisciplinary evidence, scientific independence, transparent communication, early intervention, and recognition of social determinants in neurological epidemics. These lessons remain highly relevant as Cuba today confronts renewed economic hardship and disturbing geopolitical challenges in progress.

articles.title: Adjunctive gabexate mesylate with octreotide and clinical outcomes in older adults with acute pancreatitis: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute pancreatitis (AP) in older adults is associated with higher risks of systemic inflammatory response, organ dysfunction, and prolonged clinical recovery. Pharmacologic interventions targeting early protease activation and exocrine pancreatic secretion may have therapeutic value in this population; however, evidence in elderly patients remains limited. METHODS: This retrospective study included 220 adults aged ≥60 years hospitalized with AP between July 2021 and July 2025. Among them, 108 received octreotide plus gabexate mesylate and 112 received octreotide monotherapy. Primary outcomes were times to abdominal pain relief, pancreatic enzyme normalization, and gastrointestinal recovery. Multiple linear and multivariable logistic regression models were used to adjust for prespecified demographic and clinical covariates. RESULTS: Combination therapy was associated with shorter times to abdominal pain relief (adjusted mean difference -0.95 days; 95% confidence interval [CI] -1.28 to -0.62), pancreatic enzyme normalization (-1.28 days; 95% CI, -1.67 to -0.89), gastrointestinal recovery (-0.86 days; 95% CI -1.25 to -0.47), and hospital discharge (-1.62 days; 95% CI, -2.47 to -0.77; all P ≤ 0.001). It was also associated with higher odds of radiological improvement among re-imaged patients (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 1.82; 95% CI, 1.16-2.86) and lower odds of new-onset or persistent systemic inflammatory response syndrome (adjusted OR, 0.61; 95% CI, 0.38-0.98) and infectious complications (adjusted OR, 0.54; 95% CI, 0.29-0.99). Drug-related adverse events, composite organ dysfunction, mortality, and readmission did not differ significantly. No treatment-by-severity interaction was identified. CONCLUSION: Adjunctive gabexate mesylate was associated with modestly faster short-term recovery in older adults with acute pancreatitis, without a significant increase in drug-related adverse events. Its effects on organ dysfunction and mortality remain uncertain and require confirmation in prospective randomized studies.

articles.title: Dendrobium officinale polysaccharides ameliorate radiation-induced premature ovarian insufficiency through coordinated modulation involving the gut microbiota-PI3K/AKT-glycolysis axis.
articles.abstract: Radiotherapy-induced premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) remains a clinical challenge with limited preventative strategies. Dendrobium officinale polysaccharides (DOP) exhibit beneficial bioactivities, but their efficacy and mechanism against radiation-induced POI are unknown. In this study, a mouse model of POI was established by single-dose whole-body X-ray irradiation (5 Gy). Mice were pretreated with a partially purified DOP preparation (500 mg/kg/day) for 7 days prior to and 14 days post-irradiation. Ovarian function was assessed via estrous cyclicity, hormone assays, histomorphology, and follicle counting. Mechanisms were investigated through analysis of apoptosis (TUNEL, IHC, flow cytometry), PI3K/AKT signaling and glycolysis-related marker expression (qPCR, IF, Western blot), and gut microbiota (16S rRNA sequencing), with in vitro validation using irradiated human granulosa cells (KGN). DOP pretreatment significantly attenuated POI phenotypes, restoring estrous cyclicity, improving serum sex hormone profiles (increased E2 and AMH; decreased FSH and LH), and preserving ovarian/uterine morphology and follicle pool. Mechanistically, DOP inhibited ovarian granulosa cell apoptosis in vivo and in vitro, concomitant with reduced ROS levels. Immunofluorescence and qPCR analyses revealed that DOP modulated the PI3K/AKT pathway in growing follicles while suppressing its overactivation in primordial follicles, as evidenced by modulated expression and localization of FOXO3a and rps6 and increased phosphorylation of AKT, mTOR, FOXO3a, and rps6. Concurrently, DOP upregulated the expression of glycolysis-related markers including GLUT4, HK1, PKM2, and LDHA at both mRNA and protein levels. Furthermore, DOP restored gut microbiota diversity and composition altered by irradiation, increasing the abundance of beneficial taxa such as Muribaculum. Collectively, these findings suggest that DOP exerts a protective effect against radiation-induced POI through a multi-targeted mechanism involving anti-apoptosis, modulation of PI3K/AKT signaling and glycolysis-related marker expression in growing follicles, inhibition of primordial follicle overactivation, and remediation of gut dysbiosis. These findings position DOP as a promising natural candidate for improving ovarian injury-related parameters, warranting further investigation.

articles.title: Integrating knowledge graphs and retrieval-augmented generation to identify clinical pharmacology gaps in infectious disease trial protocols.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Clinical trial protocols contain critical clinical pharmacology information that is often scattered across different sections of these lengthy documents. The purpose was to evaluate whether a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) protocol review integrated with knowledge graphs (KGs) could be used to obtain clinical pharmacology evidence and identify regulatory gaps. METHODS: Clinical trial protocols were obtained from the Gates Foundation's publicly available corpus of clinical trials in low- and middle-income countries. The RAG protocol review was used to assess the protocols against Food & Drug Administration (FDA) guidance documents for hepatic impairment, exposure-response, population PK (PopPK), and physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling (PBPK). Disease-specific KG analyses were conducted for tuberculosis (TB), human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), malaria, and neglected tropical diseases (NTD). KG models connecting studies to drugs, diseases, pharmacologic classes, organ-function exclusions, biomarkers, and pharmacokinetic (PK) parameter features were obtained. RESULTS: Across 42 unique trials, the KG contained 223 nodes and 376 edges. TB protocols produced the largest disease-specific graph, whereas HIV had the highest frequency of PK studies. Gap analysis showed that hepatic impairment exclusions in TB were more frequent than PK studies. In the multi-guidance evaluation, faithfulness was high, answer relevancy was lower, and the clinical pharmacology metric showed guidance-dependent differences. CONCLUSION: The integrated KG-RAG approach can help highlight potential gaps in clinical pharmacology reporting in infectious disease clinical trial protocols.

articles.title: Bioequivalence study of two formulations of a sitagliptin/metformin hydrochloride extended-release tablet in healthy Chinese subjects under fasting and fed conditions: a randomized, open-label, single-dose, crossover trial.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: This study aimed to evaluate the bioequivalence and safety of a newly developed generic sitagliptin/metformin hydrochloride extended-release (XR) tablet (50 mg/500 mg) compared with the reference formulation, Janumet XR, in healthy Chinese subjects under fasting and fed conditions. METHODS: This randomized, open-label, single-dose, two-period, two-sequence crossover study included 40 subjects in the fasting cohort and 36 subjects in the fed cohort. Subjects received a single dose of the test or reference formulation in each period, separated by a 5-day washout period. Plasma concentrations of sitagliptin and metformin were determined using a validated liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry method. Bioequivalence was assessed using the 90% confidence intervals (CIs) for the geometric mean ratios (GMRs; test/reference) of maximum plasma concentration (Cmax), area under the plasma concentration-time curve from time zero to the last quantifiable concentration (AUC0-t), and area under the plasma concentration-time curve from time zero to infinity (AUC0-infinity). RESULTS: Under fasting conditions, the 90% CIs for the GMRs of sitagliptin for Cmax, AUC0-t, and AUC0-infinity were 88.24%-101.46%, 98.24%-103.15%, and 98.41%-103.33%, respectively. The corresponding values for metformin were 93.23%-103.26%, 93.00%-106.20%, and 92.89%-105.74%. Bioequivalence was also established under fed conditions for sitagliptin (Cmax: 88.29%-99.06%; AUC0-t: 96.19%-101.02%; AUC0-infinity: 96.07%-101.04%) and metformin (Cmax: 92.06% -99.39%; AUC0-t: 91.31%-100.06%; AUC0-infinity: 91.00%-99.30%). Analysis of variance showed a significant period effect for metformin AUC0-t and AUC0-infinity under fasting conditions (P < 0.05), whereas no significant formulation effect was observed (P > 0.05). Both formulations were well tolerated. Only Grade 1 or Grade 2 adverse events were reported, and no serious adverse events occurred. DISCUSSION: The generic sitagliptin/metformin hydrochloride XR tablet was bioequivalent to the reference product under both fasting and fed conditions in healthy Chinese subjects. The generic formulation was well tolerated and may provide a safe and effective alternative for the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

articles.title: Aloysia deserticola (rica-rica) essential oil impairs inhibitory synaptic transmission in hippocampal CA1 pyramidal neurons.
articles.abstract: Aloysia deserticola is an aromatic plant native to the Chilean Andean highlands that has traditionally been used in herbal preparations. Although a previous behavioral study reported the anxiolytic and antidepressant-like effects of rica-rica essential oil in an animal model, its neurophysiological actions at cellular and synaptic levels remain largely unexplored. In this study, we characterized A. deserticola essential oil (AD-EO) using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) and examined its acute effects on GABAergic synaptic transmission via whole-cell patch-clamp recordings from CA1 pyramidal neurons in acute dorsal hippocampal slices obtained from C57BL/6 J mice. GC-MS analysis revealed an enriched thujone chemical profile, with peaks tentatively identified as α- and β-thujone accounting for 89.06% and 3.38% of the total chromatographic area, respectively. Application of AD-EO to the bath reduced evoked inhibitory postsynaptic current (eIPSC) amplitude in a concentration-dependent manner and shortened eIPSC decay kinetics. This is consistent with a postsynaptic contribution to the suppression of inhibitory signaling. At intermediate-to-high estimated thujone-equivalent concentrations, AD-EO increased the paired-pulse ratio. Coefficient-of-variation analysis supported the presence of an additional presynaptic component. Consistent with these findings, AD-EO reduced the frequency and amplitude of miniature inhibitory postsynaptic currents. Furthermore, the effects on eIPSC amplitude and the paired-pulse ratio were reversible following washout. Together, these results demonstrate that AD-EO suppresses inhibitory synapses in CA1 pyramidal neurons via effects consistent with pre- and postsynaptic locus. These results provide electrophysiological evidence that AD-EO modulates hippocampal inhibitory transmission and support further investigation of the mechanisms underlying the neurophysiological actions of this complex natural preparation.

articles.title: Effect of mucosal hydration on time-dependent mucoadhesion of polymeric nanocomposite microspheres to ovine nasal mucosa: relationship to swelling kinetics.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mucoadhesion of hydrophilic polymeric carriers is strongly influenced by hydration, which promotes polymer-chain mobility and facilitates interactions with mucin. However, excessive hydration may compromise the mechanical integrity of the adhesive interface. This study investigated the temporal relationship between swelling kinetics and nasal mucoadhesion of polymeric nanocomposite microsphere systems under different mucosal hydration conditions. METHODS: Two polymeric nanocomposite microsphere systems, IDB-MS and DFP-MS, were evaluated for swelling over 40 min using standardized compacted microsphere discs and for adhesion to excised ovine nasal mucosa under native/quasi-dry and highly hydrated conditions. Adhesion tension was determined over contact times ranging from 1 to 25 min. The effects of formulation and time on swelling and those of formulation, mucosal hydration, and contact time on adhesion tension were evaluated using factorial ANOVA. RESULTS: Both systems showed comparable swelling kinetics, reaching their maximum experimentally observed swelling at 5 min (465.96% for IDB-MS and 470.00% for DFP-MS), with no significant main effect of formulation. Mucoadhesion was strongly affected by mucosal hydration and contact time, whereas formulation had no significant main effect. Adhesion tension was consistently higher under native/quasi-dry than under highly hydrated mucosal conditions. Spline interpolation estimated the time of maximum adhesion at approximately 4.0-4.5 min, whereas the highest experimentally measured adhesion tension occurred at the 5-min sampling point. However, the post-maximum decline in adhesion preceded the corresponding decrease in apparent swelling, particularly under highly hydrated conditions. CONCLUSION: Polymer swelling and mucoadhesion showed condition-dependent temporal correspondence, but swelling alone was insufficient to explain adhesive strength. The results support the hypothesis that mucoadhesion may depend on a balance between sufficient polymer hydration and preservation of interfacial cohesion; however, the present comparison of two hydration conditions does not establish an optimal hydration level. Mucosal hydration should therefore be considered an important experimental parameter in the evaluation of nasal mucoadhesive drug-delivery systems.

articles.title: Cardiac adverse event signals of Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitors as primary suspect and in co-reported regimens: a large-scale FAERS pharmacovigilance study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitors (BTKis) have improved outcomes in B-cell malignancies, but cardiac toxicity remains a clinically relevant concern, particularly with newer-generation agents and co-reported regimens. We aimed to characterize real-world cardiac adverse event signals associated with BTKis as primary suspect (PS) agents and in co-reported regimens. METHODS: We conducted a pharmacovigilance study using the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System from the fourth quarter of 2013 to the first quarter of 2025. We evaluated BTKi regimens (ibrutinib, acalabrutinib, and zanubrutinib as primary suspect agents) and three specific BTKi-based co-reported combination subgroups (BTKi + anti-CD20 monoclonal antibodies, BTKi + venetoclax, and BTKi + lenalidomide). Cardiac adverse events were defined by the Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities "Cardiac disorders" system organ class. Disproportionality signals were assessed using four algorithms, and time-to-onset and fatal-case phenotypes were evaluated. RESULTS: A total of 8,266 BTKi-associated cardiac adverse event reports were identified. "Cardiac disorders" showed consistent disproportionality signals across BTKis. Ibrutinib had the broadest cardiac signal spectrum, whereas acalabrutinib and zanubrutinib showed fewer but earlier-onset cardiac events. Median reported time-to-onset was 150 days for ibrutinib, 72.5 days for acalabrutinib, and 66 days for zanubrutinib. Among co-reported regimens, BTKi plus lenalidomide showed the strongest disproportional reporting signal for atrial fibrillation. Reports with fatal cardiac outcome were more frequently reported among males, patients older than 85 years, and events occurring within 30 days of treatment initiation. CONCLUSION: BTKis exhibit distinct real-world cardiac safety profiles. Early cardiovascular surveillance may be particularly important for newer-generation BTKis and BTKi-lenalidomide co-reported regimens, especially in patients with risk factors associated with higher reporting proportions.

articles.title: Blockade of the calpain-1/HSP90/TGF-β1 axis by Astragaloside IV ameliorates bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Previous studies have confirmed the therapeutic potential of Astragaloside IV (AS-IV) in pulmonary fibrosis, yet the upstream regulatory mechanisms governing TGF-β1 stability, particularly involving proteolytic enzymes, are not fully understood. This study investigates the pivotal role of calpain-1 in modulating the HSP90/TGF-β1 signaling pathway, thereby elucidating the effects of AS-IV on bleomycin (BLM)-induced pulmonary fibrosis. METHODS: Calpain-1 knockout (CAPN1-/-) and wild-type (WT) mice were used to establish pulmonary fibrosis models via intratracheal instillation of BLM. Both animal and cell models were administered varying doses of AS-IV for intervention. Inflammatory, oxidative stress, fibrotic, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) markers were subsequently evaluated. Additionally, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) experiments were employed to assess the binding interactions between AS-IV and the calpain-1/HSP90/TGF-β1 axis. RESULTS: The calpain-1/HSP90/TGF-β1 axis was significantly activated in BLM-induced pulmonary fibrosis mice. AS-IV ameliorated pulmonary fibrosis, EMT, oxidative stress, and inflammation while simultaneously suppressing this overactivated axis. Calpain-1 knockout inhibited HSP90 upregulation, attenuated TGF-β1/Smad2/3 activation, and reduced pulmonary fibrosis. In vivo experiments further confirmed the inhibitory effects of AS-IV and calpain-1 inhibition on lung epithelial cell injury and fibroblast proliferation. Notably, calpain-1 overexpression in MLE-12 cells abolished the protective effects of AS-IV against EMT, oxidative stress, and inflammation. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and SPR experiments confirmed the direct binding between AS-IV and calpain-1, supporting its upstream regulatory role in this signaling axis. CONCLUSION: AS-IV attenuates pulmonary fibrosis by targeting calpain-1 to disrupt the HSP90/TGF-β1 signaling axis. These findings identify calpain-1 as a novel therapeutic target and support AS-IV as a promising candidate for PF treatment.

articles.title: Sustained release of metformin through an injectable hydrogel for synergistic macrophage reprogramming and ROS scavenging in the analgesic treatment of osteoarthritis.
articles.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA), a prevalent joint disorder affecting millions worldwide, is primarily characterized by chronic pain driven by synovial M1-polarized macrophages, which perpetuate inflammation and generate excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS). However, existing pharmacological treatments offer limited long-term efficacy. Metformin, a known modulator of M1 macrophage polarization and ROS production, has demonstrated efficacy in alleviating OA pain via oral administration. Yet, its therapeutic translation is hindered by poor joint tissue bioavailability. Intra-articular (IA) delivery offers a clinically attractive solution, achieving high local drug concentrations while minimizing systemic exposure, but conventional IA formulations are rapidly cleared from the joint space, restricting their efficacy. We designed an injectable hydrogel based on dopamine (DA) and carboxyl-terminated Pluronic F127 (F127) and crosslinked the hydrogel network via oxidative coupling between catechol groups using an H2O2/horseradish peroxidase (HRP) system (termed 'F127-DA-HRP') to deliver metformin (termed 'Met-F127-DA-HRP') intra-articularly in a sustained manner. The Met-F127-DA-HRP hydrogel scavenges ROS through its catechol groups and sustained metformin release, while also promoting M1-to-M2 macrophage repolarization and suppressing inflammatory cytokines. Importantly, a single IA injection of Met-F127-DA-HRP hydrogel maintained 2-fold higher metformin concentrations in joint tissues compared to Met-F127 hydrogel, with sustained retention for up to 30 days. In monosodium iodoacetate (MIA)-induced OA, IA injection of Met-F127-DA-HRP hydrogel successfully relieved OA pain and ameliorated synovitis with long-lasting effects. Collectively, this work introduces a potent therapeutic strategy for the sustained management of OA pain by utilizing an injectable hydrogel to prolong the IA residency of metformin, offering long-acting IA analgesia through macrophage-directed immunomodulation.

articles.title: Top-down evaluation of measurement uncertainty from validation data including sampling.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Measurement uncertainty is essential for reliable pharmaceutical quality control and conformity assessment. However, conventional top-down approaches generally estimate uncertainty from validation data considering analytical variability, while uncertainty arising from sampling is frequently neglected. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop a practical top-down approach for evaluating measurement uncertainty from validation data that explicitly incorporates sampling uncertainty according to the principles of the Eurachem Validation of Measurement Procedures that Include Sampling (VaMPIS) guide. METHODS: Precision was evaluated using a crossed-nested analysis of variance design involving target samples, independent replicate samples, intermediate precision conditions, and analytical replicates, enabling estimation of variance components associated with sampling, intermediate precision, and analytical repeatability. The trueness contribution to uncertainty was estimated from recovery studies. An MS-Excel workbook with automated routines was developed to support validation protocols and uncertainty calculations. The approach was applied to the assay of furosemide tablets by UV spectrophotometry and ibuprofen oral suspension by high-performance liquid chromatography. RESULTS: Combined standard uncertainties of 3.4% and 3.1% were obtained for the furosemide and ibuprofen methods, respectively. The relative contributions to the uncertainty budget differed between the two procedures, while analytical repeatability contributed only marginally in both cases. The breakdown of precision uncertainty identified the principal sources of variability and supported targeted optimization strategies. Comparison with a target standard uncertainty of 3.2%, derived from the assay specification according to WHO recommendations, demonstrated the practical impact of including sampling in the uncertainty evaluation. CONCLUSION: The proposed approach provides a practical framework for integrating sampling uncertainty into pharmaceutical method validation, supporting Analytical Quality by Design principles and improving the reliability of conformity assessment and regulatory decision-making.

articles.title: Effects of Perfluorohexane Sulfonic Acid on Female Reproductive Function and Oocyte Quality.
articles.abstract: An emerging persistent organic pollutant, perfluorohexane sulfonic acid (PFHxS), has drawn considerable attention owing to its female reproductive toxicity. PFHxS penetrates the blood-follicle barrier and accumulates in follicular fluid, with a prolonged elimination half-life in humans. Mechanistically, PFHxS impairs oocyte quality through oxidative stress, mitochondrial damage, disruption of hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis signaling, meiotic spindle abnormalities, and epigenetic modifications. Animal models demonstrate that PFHxS exposure leads to follicular arrest, reduced ovulation, and intrauterine growth restriction in offspring. Human studies have associated exposure with diminished ovarian reserve, prolonged amenorrhea, and reduced high-quality embryos. Current research highlights a shift from single-compound to mixture effects and transgenerational epigenetic inheritance, yet significant gaps remain regarding chronic low-dose exposure and causal evidence in clinical populations. Future research should focus on realistic exposure models and large-scale prospective cohorts, and the existing evidence should be integrated into regulatory frameworks to safeguard reproductive health.

articles.title: Bictegravir/Lenacapavir: A 2-Drug Regimen for the Treatment of HIV-1 Infection.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of bictegravir/lenacapavir for the treatment of HIV-1 infection. DATA SOURCES: A literature search was conducted in PubMed and Google Scholar (January 2016-August 2026) using the search terms bictegravir and lenacapavir. Other data sources included abstracts presented at recent conferences and the prescribing information. STUDY SELECTION AND DATA EXTRACTION: All English-language studies assessing the efficacy and safety of bictegravir/lenacapavir for the treatment of HIV-1 infection were considered for inclusion. DATA SYNTHESIS: Bictegravir is an established second-generation integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI), whereas lenacapavir is a novel capsid inhibitor. Both antiretrovirals are highly active against HIV-1. Bictegravir/lenacapavir 75 mg/50 mg was shown to be safe and effective in two phase 3 clinical trials after switching from complex antiretroviral therapy (ART) or bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide. The Food and Drug Administration approved this combination for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in adults who are virologically suppressed on stable ART with no resistance to the individual components. It is available as a single-tablet regimen (STR) taken orally once daily.Relevance to Patient Care and Clinical Practice in Comparison With Existing Drugs:Bictegravir/lenacapvir is the first INSTI-capsid inhibitor 2-drug STR indicated for the treatment of HIV-1 infection. The combination could be useful for patients who want to simplify their regimen and/or those who cannot use a nucleos(t)ide or a non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor. It is not active against hepatitis B virus coinfection. CONCLUSIONS: Bictegravir/lenacapvir is safe and efficacious as a 2-drug regimen for the treatment of adults with HIV-1 infection.

articles.title: From Itch to Innovation: The Emerging Role of Remibrutinib in Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This article reviews the published data encompassing the development, pharmacology, efficacy, and safety of remibrutinib, summarizing data from pivotal clinical studies and clinical relevance in the treatment of chronic spontaneous urticaria. DATA SOURCES: A literature review was conducted in PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov from inception through August 2026, using terms "RHAPSIDO," "remibrutinib," "LOU064," and "chronic spontaneous urticaria." Articles from reference lists were included to identify potentially relevant literature. STUDY SELECTION AND DATA EXTRACTION: Clinical data and studies were limited to those published in the English language that discussed the safety and efficacy of remibrutinib. DATA SYNTHESIS: The pivotal phase III studies REMIX-1 (n = 470) and REMIX-2 (n = 455) met all primary endpoints at week 12, with Urticaria Activity Score over 7 days (UAS7) reductions of -20.02 and -19.41 versus -13.79 and -11.73 with placebo, parallel improvements in itch and hive severity, and complete absence of itch and hives in 31.1% and 27.9% versus 10.5% and 6.5%. Safety was comparable to placebo, with mild mucocutaneous bleeding (mainly petechiae) the only category significantly more frequent.Relevance to Patient Care and Clinical Practice in Comparison to Existing Drugs:As the first approved oral targeted Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitor, remibrutinib provides a new therapeutic option in chronic spontaneous urticaria treatment. Clinical practice is improved by the broadened evidence-based management option, which offers an oral pill alternative with no required routine lab monitoring in place of biologic injections. CONCLUSION: Remibrutinib provides a new treatment option with the ability to control symptoms and improve quality of life for patients with difficult-to-treat chronic spontaneous urticaria.

articles.title: A Pilot Study to Describe Symptomatic Hyperammonemia Secondary to Recombinant Erwinia Asparaginase.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Asparaginase therapy is essential for the treatment of pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (ALL/LLy). For patients who develop hypersensitivity to a first-line Escherichia coli (E. coli)-derived product, the standard of care is to transition to an Erwinia-derived product. Given that all asparaginase products exert their antileukemic effects by enzymatically breaking down asparagine to aspartic acid and ammonia, elevations in ammonia levels are anticipated during asparaginase treatment. However, symptomatic hyperammonemia is not expected. Recombinant Erwinia asparaginase is relatively new to the market, and there have been several case reports of symptomatic hyperammonemia with this specific formulation. OBJECTIVES: The primary objective of this prospective study was to establish the incidence of symptomatic hyperammonemia secondary to recombinant Erwinia asparaginase and to determine if a larger, multicenter trial was warranted. Additional objectives included identifying potential risk factors for symptomatic hyperammonemia. METHODS: This single-center, prospective trial received institutional review board approval. Funding was provided by the Mayo Clinic Clinical and Translational Science Award (grant number: UL1TR002377) and the Mayo Clinic Department of Pharmacy. All patients treated by the pediatric hematology/oncology team at our institution who were receiving recombinant Erwinia asparaginase were eligible. Patients were excluded if they were less than 1 year of age at study entry. Enrolled participants had a baseline plasma ammonia level obtained, followed by twice weekly ammonia levels while receiving recombinant Erwinia asparaginase. Aside from baseline, all ammonia levels were trough levels measured either 48 h or 72 h after the previous dose. RESULTS: Five patients were included, three of whom were male (60%). Three patients had T-cell ALL (60%), one patient had B-cell ALL (20%), and one patient had infantile B-cell ALL (20%). The median age was 5 years (range 1-14). Two patients were followed for two courses of recombinant Erwinia asparaginase, and the remaining patients were followed for a single course. Median baseline plasma ammonia level was 12 μmol/L. Median ammonia level while receiving recombinant Erwinia asparaginase was 146 μmol/L. Three patients (60%) developed symptomatic hyperammonemia with a median ammonia level of 174 μmol/L (range 108-343). The reported symptoms were nausea (100%), fatigue (66.7%), and decreased appetite (33.3%). The remaining two patients experienced asymptomatic hyperammonemia with a median ammonia level of 125 μmol/L (range 55-304). CONCLUSIONS: Based on our small cohort, symptomatic hyperammonemia may be a common adverse effect for patients receiving recombinant Erwinia asparaginase. Evaluating plasma ammonia levels appears reasonable in patients who are experiencing nausea or other symptoms of hyperammonemia. Additional studies are warranted to further characterize this toxicity.

articles.title: "Chitosan-Carrageenan Nanocarriers Potentiate Anticancer Efficacy of Laxmitaru against Triple-Negative Breast Cancer".
articles.abstract: Objective - Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) requires new targeted therapies with low toxicity. This study aimed to enhance therapeutic efficacy of Simarouba glauca DC also called Laxmitaru (LX), limited by poor solubility, by developing novel nanoformulation to overcome these pharmaceutical barriers.Significance - This work addresses need for effective TNBC treatments by combining a natural product with nanotechnology. Approach offers biocompatible strategy to significantly improve anticancer action of LX, potentially providing targeted alternative to conventional therapies.Methods - LX encapsulated within chitosan-carrageenan nanoparticles (LX-CC-NPs), formulation characterized for particle size, zeta potential, and physical state. Its anticancer efficacy was evaluated against HCC-70 TNBC cells using MTT assays, also comparing it to free LX and on MCF-10A.Results - Successful encapsulation yielded nanocarriers with increased size of 355.8 nm and positive surface charge of +33.25 mV, transitioned to an amorphous state, favouring drug release. In vitro, LX-CC-NPs exhibited cytotoxicity against HCC-70 cells (IC50 = 74.60 µg/mL; 82.50% inhibition at 200 µg/mL) and demonstrated biocompatibility towards MCF-10A cells, confirming a favourable therapeutic window.Conclusions - Nanoencapsulation effectively overcomes physicochemical limitations of LX, profoundly enhancing its anticancer potency and selectivity against TNBC cells. This work presents promising biocompatible nanomedicine for targeted TNBC therapy.

articles.title: Targeting cGMP pathways: the impact of vericiguat and high intensity interval training on mammary cancer progression in female mice.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND & OBJECTIVES: Recent studies confirmed the involvement of the cGMP pathway in regulating tumorigenesis. This research assessed the effect of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) and Vericiguat on the cGMP pathway in a BALB/c mouse model of mammary cancer. METHODS: Seventy BALB/C female mice were randomly divided into seven groups: Healthy Control (CON), PBS, Cancer (CA), Cancer+Exercise (CA + EX), Cancer+Vericiguat (CA + VER), Cancer+Vehicle (CA + V), and Cancer+Exercise+Vericiguat (CA + EX+VER). The cancer groups received injections of 4T1 cells to induce mammary tumors. Following tumor induction, the exercise groups performed 6 weeks of HIIT, which consisted of running at 80-95% of Vmax, 4-10 intervals, and five sessions per week, and drug groups received 0.5 mg/kg Vericiguat. RESULTS & CONCLUSION: The protein expression of sGC, PKG, cGMP, and BAX in breast tumor tissue was lower, while Bcl2, Cyclin D1, and Survivin were higher in CA compared with CON. However, EX, VER, and their combination increased the expression of sGC, PKG, cGMP, and BAX, and decreased the expression of Cyclin D1, Bcl2, and Survivin. Tumor volume decreased in all treated groups compared to the CA group in weeks 3-8. These findings suggest that the combination of EX and VER may be a promising therapeutic strategy for mammary cancer treatment by modulating cGMP signaling.

articles.title: Combined vitamins C and E attenuate memory impairment and hippocampal damage in diabetic sleep-deprived mice: behavioral and molecular insights.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Diabetes mellitus (DM) and sleep disturbances are associated with cognitive impairment and hippocampal dysfunction, potentially involving oxidative stress and neuroinflammation. OBJECTIVE: This study investigated the effects of vitamins C and E, individually and in combination, to determine whether their complementary antioxidant properties provide enhanced neuroprotective effects against cognitive and hippocampal alterations in diabetic sleep-deprived mice. METHODS: Diabetes was induced in male BALB/c mice (25-30 g) by streptozotocin (60 mg/kg), followed by partial sleep deprivation using the inverted flowerpot method. Animals received vitamin C (50 mg/kg), vitamin E (100 mg/kg), or their combination for 20 days. Body weight and blood glucose were monitored. Spatial learning and memory were evaluated using the Morris water maze. Hippocampal histopathology, GFAP immunostaining, and expression of genes related to oxidative stress, inflammation, and neuroprotection were assessed. RESULTS: Vitamin E and combined vitamin C and E treatment reduced FBG and were associated with higher final body weight than untreated diabetic sleep-deprived mice. Vitamin treatments improved spatial learning and memory, with combined treatment producing greater improvements in selected behavioral outcomes. Combined treatment increased hippocampal neuronal density and reduced GFAP immunoreactivity. Vitamin treatment increased BDNF, Nrf2, and HO-1 expression and reduced iNOS, TNF-α, and IL-1β expression. CONCLUSION: Vitamin C and E, particularly in combination, were associated with improved metabolic, cognitive, and hippocampal outcomes in diabetic sleep-deprived mice, potentially involving modulation of neuroinflammatory and oxidative stress-related markers.

articles.title: Comparative antidiabetic efficacy of Murraya koenigii extract and myricetin-derived copper nanoparticles.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Green synthesis of copper-containing nanoparticles (CuNPs) using plant-derived bioactive compounds is a promising approach for developing potential antidiabetic nanotherapeutics. However, the influence of purified phytochemicals, compared with crude plant extracts, on nanoparticle characteristics and antidiabetic efficacy requires further investigation. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare the physicochemical characteristics and antidiabetic efficacy of CuNPs synthesized using Murraya koenigii leaf extract and its isolated flavonoid, myricetin. METHODS: Myricetin was isolated from M. Koenigii and identified and quantified using high-performance thin-layer chromatography (HPTLC), with UV-Visible spectrophotometry used for further characterization. The synthesized cunps were characterized using UV-Visible spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), dynamic light scattering (DLS), zeta potential analysis, and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS). Antidiabetic efficacy was evaluated in streptozotocin-induced diabetic male Wistar rats over 21 days. RESULTS: SEM analysis revealed apparent particle or agglomerate dimensions of 100-450 nm for M. Koenigii-derived cunps, whereas TEM showed predominantly spherical myricetin-derived CuNPs with dimensions of 22-51 nm. DLS analysis showed a hydrodynamic diameter of 237.0 nm and a polydispersity index (PDI) of 0.375 for myricetin-derived cunps, compared with a PDI of 0.454 for M. Koenigii-derived CuNPs. Myricetin-derived CuNPs exhibited a zeta potential of - 26.9 mv. After 21 days of treatment, the mean blood glucose level in the myricetin-derived CuNPs group decreased to 90.25 ± 6.88 mg/dl, compared with 110.68 mg/dl in the free-myricetin group, 119.25 mg/dl in the M. Koenigii-derived CuNPs group, 125.25 mg/dl in the M. Koenigii extract group, and 103.68 mg/dl in the glibenclamide-treated group. CONCLUSION: Myricetin-derived CuNPs demonstrated promising antidiabetic activity in streptozotocin-induced diabetic rats and exhibited a comparatively narrower particle-size distribution than M. Koenigii-derived CuNPs. These findings support further investigation of phytochemical-guided CuNPs synthesis for potential antidiabetic applications.

articles.title: Virtual screening, synthesis, solid state characterization, evaluation for solubility, dissolution, and stability of gallic acid-based cocrystals of glimepiride.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Glimepiride is a second generation Sulfonylurea class of antidiabetic drug. It belongs to BCS Class-II with a varying dissolution profile and bioavailability on account of limited aqueous solubility. The present study aimed to alter and improve physicochemical properties of glimepiride by modifying its crystal lattice through co-processing the same with an inert carrier like gallic acid to form cocrystals. OBJECTIVE: The present study deals with rational approach to select coformer for Co-crystallization of Glimepiride, followed by its confirmation by solid state characterization using FTIR, DSC and PXRD studies. Cocrystal formation and its effect on solubility, in-vitro drug release and stability were also evaluated. METHODS: Gallic acid was selected as coformer through multiple virtual screening methods such as COSMO-RS, Hansen solubility parameter (HSP), and pKa method. Cocrystal was formulated by solvent assisted grinding method using methanol and characterized by Fourier-transform spectroscopy (FTIR), Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), Powder X-ray diffraction method (PXRD), and Solid state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy (ssNMR) to identify the solid-state modification. Equilibrium solubility and in-vitro dissolution study were accomplished to estimate the solubility and dissolution behavior of cocrystals in comparison to pure drug. The drug content analysis of cocrystal formulation proved no loss of API during processing while stability study showed the integrity of drug in formulation throughout the study. RESULTS: Cocrystal formation of Glimepiride with gallic acid was confirmed by spectroscopic changes in FTIR and DSC. Comparative PXRD and ssNMR study further endorsed the formation of new crystalline species. Experimental confirmation of cocrystals have proved reliability of virtual screening methods. The seven-fold rise in aqueous solubility of cocrystal formulation than that of pure drug attributed to new crystalline phase with minimum lattice energy that further contributed to drug solubility and dissolution enhancement. CONCLUSION: Co-crystallization of Glimepiride with gallic acid is simple, reliable formulation approach to alter solubility and dissolution by altering crystal lattice of drug. Thus, co-crystallization is effective method for optimizing therapeutic efficacy of Glimepiride.

articles.title: A Heuristic Framework for Comparative Deformation Mapping of Pharmaceutical Excipients Using Compaction Simulator Data.
articles.abstract: Understanding the material deformation behavior in tablet dies is crucial for pharmaceutical development, as it directly influences manufacturability and final tablet properties. Heckel analysis provides a theoretical framework for assessing material deformation during compaction, but its direct correlation with real-world tableting behavior remains an area of interest. This study introduces a framework for characterizing the deformation mechanisms of pharmaceutical powders. It addresses limitations in conventional methods that rely solely on yield pressure (Py) and strain rate sensitivity (SRS), which fail to fully differentiate elastic and plastic deformation. The heuristic framework for comparative deformation mapping enables differentiation of excipients across the brittle-plastic-elastic space using two parameters from a compaction simulator: Py (from Heckel analysis) and pressure drop (ΔP, from an in-die stress relaxation test). ΔP is treated as a descriptor of time-dependent (viscoplastic and viscoelastic) deformation rather than as a direct measure of elasticity, and its use as an empirical surrogate for elastic character was benchmarked against independent force-displacement elastic energy. Applied to ten common pharmaceutical excipients, the framework differentiated materials that Py and SRS alone did not resolve (SRS was determined for the four reference materials). Across the ten materials, ΔP tracked elastic energy mainly between excipient classes, whereas within the six lactose grades the relationship was reversed, indicating that ΔP differences within a class reflect time-dependent deformation. The framework is therefore proposed as a comparative, material-sparing screening tool for early-stage excipient selection, not as a predictor of tableting performance or scale-up behavior.

articles.title: Efficacy, Safety, and Impact of Combined Extended-Release Tramadol Hydrochloride and Acetaminophen on Inflammatory Mediators in Malignant Lymphoma-Associated Pain.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Malignant lymphoma-associated pain significantly impairs quality of life and is linked to systemic inflammatory responses. This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of combining extended-release tramadol hydrochloride with acetaminophen compared with monotherapy. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of tramadol hydrochloride extended-release tablets in combination with acetaminophen versus monotherapy with either agent in the treatment of malignant lymphoma-related pain, and to investigate the effects of these treatment regimens on peripheral pain mediators and systemic inflammatory cytokines. METHODS: A comparative study was conducted involving 165 patients with malignant lymphoma-associated pain (January 2024-December 2025). Patients were assigned to 3 groups: acetaminophen (n = 53), tramadol (n = 55), or combination therapy (n = 57), receiving 28 days of treatment. Primary outcomes included Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) pain scores and analgesic efficacy. Secondary outcomes included peripheral blood pain mediators (substance P [SP], prostaglandin E2 [PGE2], endothelin-1 [ET-1], 5-hydroxytryptamine [5-HT]), inflammatory cytokines (interleukin [IL]-2, IL-4, IL-6, IL-10, tumor necrosis factor-α [TNF-α]], interferon-γ [IFN-γγ]), and quality of life. RESULTS: The combination group demonstrated significantly greater reductions in NRS scores and superior analgesic efficacy (91.23%) compared with acetaminophen (71.70%) and tramadol (78.18%) groups (P<0.05). Combination therapy resulted in the greatest reduction of pain mediators (SP, PGE2, ET-1, 5-HT) and significant modulation of cytokines (lower IL-2, IL-6, TNF-α, IFN-γγ; higher IL-4, IL-10) (P<0.05). Quality of life improved significantly more in the combination group (P<0.05). Adverse event incidence was comparable across groups (18.87%-22.81%; P>0.05), indicating favorable clinical safety. CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: The combination of tramadol hydrochloride extended-release tablets and acetaminophen provides superior analgesic efficacy and greater improvement in quality of life compared with either monotherapy in the treatment of malignant lymphoma-related pain, and its mechanism is associated with the synergistic downregulation of peripheral pain mediators and modulation of the inflammatory cytokine profile. During the treatment period, the combination regimen did not significantly increase the risk of adverse reactions, demonstrating a favorable benefit-risk ratio. This report is the first to simultaneously confirm, in this patient population, both the clinical efficacy of this combination regimen and its modulatory effects on the systemic pain-inflammation network, thereby providing a strategy for enhanced analgesia in clinical practice. Based on the data from this study, this regimen may serve as an effective option for the short-term management of moderate to severe pain in patients with malignant lymphoma; however, its long-term efficacy and broad applicability require further investigation.
